bookInfo.name: Comprehensive Mirror in Aid of Governance
bookInfo.author: Sima Guang

sentences.zh: 起玄黓涒灘，盡柔兆閹茂，凡十五年。

translations.literal: From Xuanyi Tuantan through Rouzhao Yanmao; fifteen years in all.
translations.idiomatic: From Xuanyi Tuantan through Rouzhao Yanmao—fifteen years in all.

sentences.zh: 1冬，十一月，上行幸代。

translations.literal: 1. In winter, the eleventh month, the emperor traveled in person to Dai.
translations.idiomatic: 1. In winter, the eleventh month, the emperor traveled in person to Dai.

sentences.zh: ----2春，正月，自代還。

translations.literal: ----2 In spring, the first month, he returned from Dai.
translations.idiomatic: ----2 In spring, the first month, he returned from Dai.

sentences.zh: ----3夏，六月，梁懷王揖薨，無子。

translations.literal: ----3 In summer, the sixth month, King Huai of Liang bowed and died; he had no son.
translations.idiomatic: ----3 In summer, the sixth month, King Huai of Liang died; he had no son.

sentences.zh: 賈誼復上疏曰：「陛下即不定製，如今之勢，不過一傳、再傳，諸侯猶且人恣而不制，豪植而大強，漢法不得行矣。

translations.literal: Jia Yi again submitted a memorial, saying: "If Your Majesty does not at once fix institutions, under the present trend it will not pass one transmission or two before the feudal lords still do as they please without restraint, powerful houses take root and grow great, and Han law cannot be enforced.
translations.idiomatic: Jia Yi again submitted a memorial: "If Your Majesty does not at once fix institutions, under the present trend it will not pass one generation or two before the feudal lords do as they please without restraint, powerful houses take root and grow great, and Han law cannot be enforced.

sentences.zh: 陛下所以為籓扞及皇太子之所恃者，唯淮陽、代二國耳。

translations.literal: What Your Majesty relies on as feudal shield and what the crown prince depends upon is only the two states of Huaiyang and Dai.
translations.idiomatic: What Your Majesty relies on as a feudal bulwark and what the crown prince depends upon are only the two states of Huaiyang and Dai.

sentences.zh: 代，北邊匈奴，與強敵為鄰，能自完則足矣；

translations.literal: Dai, on the northern frontier with the Xiongnu and bordering a powerful foe, suffices if it can preserve itself;
translations.idiomatic: Dai, on the northern frontier with the Xiongnu and bordering a powerful foe, suffices if it can preserve itself;

sentences.zh: 而淮陽之比大諸侯，廑如黑子之著面，適足以餌大國，而不足以有所禁御。

translations.literal: yet Huaiyang compared with the great feudal lords is scant as a mole on the face—just enough to bait great states, not enough to forbid and control anything.
translations.idiomatic: yet Huaiyang beside the great feudal lords is scant as a mole on the face—just enough to bait great states, not enough to forbid or restrain them.

sentences.zh: 方今制在陛下，制國而令子適足以為餌，豈可謂工哉！

translations.literal: Now power rests with Your Majesty; to shape the realm yet make your sons barely enough for bait—how can this be called skillful!
translations.idiomatic: Power rests with Your Majesty now; to shape the realm yet make your sons barely enough for bait—how can this be called skillful!

sentences.zh: 臣之愚計，願舉淮南地以益淮陽，而為梁王立後，割淮陽北邊二、三列城與東郡以益梁。

translations.literal: Your servant's foolish plan: I wish to transfer Huainan territory to enlarge Huaiyang, establish an heir for Liang, and carve off two or three ranked cities on Huaiyang's northern border with Dong commandery to enlarge Liang.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant's plan is this: transfer Huainan territory to enlarge Huaiyang, establish an heir for Liang, and carve off two or three ranked cities on Huaiyang's northern border with Dong commandery to enlarge Liang.

sentences.zh: 不可者，可徙代王而都睢陽。

translations.literal: If that cannot be done, the king of Dai may be moved to take his capital at Suiyang.
translations.idiomatic: If that cannot be done, move the king of Dai and set his capital at Suiyang.

sentences.zh: 梁起於新郪而北著之河，淮陽包陳而南揵之江，則大諸侯之有異心者破膽而不敢謀。

translations.literal: If Liang rises from Xinqi and northward reaches the river, and Huaiyang wraps Chen and southward presses the Yangzi, then great feudal lords with other intent will break gall and not dare plot.
translations.idiomatic: If Liang rises from Xinqi and northward reaches the river, and Huaiyang wraps Chen and southward presses the Yangzi, then great feudal lords with other intent will lose heart and not dare plot.

sentences.zh: 梁足以扞齊、趙，淮陽足以禁吳、楚，陛下高枕，終無山東之憂矣，此二世之利也。

translations.literal: Liang will suffice to shield Qi and Zhao; Huaiyang will suffice to restrain Wu and Chu; Your Majesty may pillow your head high and in the end have no worry east of the mountains—this is a benefit for two generations.
translations.idiomatic: Liang will suffice to shield Qi and Zhao; Huaiyang will suffice to restrain Wu and Chu; Your Majesty may rest easy and in the end have no worry east of the mountains—this is a benefit for two generations.

sentences.zh: 當今恬然，適遇諸侯之皆少；

translations.literal: At present all is calm, just when the feudal lords are all young;
translations.idiomatic: At present all is calm, just when the feudal lords are all young;

sentences.zh: 數歲之後，陛下且見之矣。

translations.literal: after a few years Your Majesty will see it.
translations.idiomatic: after a few years Your Majesty will see it.

sentences.zh: 夫秦日夜苦心勞力以除六國之禍；

translations.literal: Qin day and night toiled in mind and body to remove the calamity of the Six States;
translations.idiomatic: Qin day and night toiled in mind and body to remove the calamity of the Six States;

sentences.zh: 今陛下力制天下，頤指如意，高拱以成六國之禍，難以言智，苟身無事，畜亂，宿祝，孰視而不定；

translations.literal: now Your Majesty by force controls all under Heaven, nods and it is as you wish, sits high with folded hands and completes the calamity of the Six States—hard to call this wisdom; if only your person is unharmed, you store disorder and lodge prayers, staring fixedly without settling;
translations.idiomatic: now Your Majesty by force controls all under Heaven, nods and it is as you wish, sits high with folded hands and completes the calamity of the Six States—hard to call this wisdom; if only your person is unharmed, you nurture disorder and lodge prayers, staring fixedly without settling policy;

sentences.zh: 萬年之後，傳之老母、弱子，將使不寧，不可謂仁。

translations.literal: after ten thousand years, passing it to an aged mother and a weak son, you will make them unquiet—this cannot be called benevolence.
translations.idiomatic: after ten thousand years, passing the realm to an aged mother and a weak son, you will make them unquiet—this cannot be called benevolence.

sentences.zh: 」帝於是從誼計，徙淮陽王武為梁王，北界泰山，西至高陽，得大縣四十餘城。

translations.literal: " The emperor thereupon followed Yi's plan, moved King Wu of Huaiyang to be king of Liang, with the northern border at Mount Tai, the western at Gaoyang, obtaining more than forty great counties.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor thereupon followed Yi's plan, moved King Wu of Huaiyang to be king of Liang, with the northern border at Mount Tai, the western at Gaoyang, obtaining more than forty great counties.

sentences.zh: 後歲餘，賈誼亦死，死時年三十三矣。

translations.literal: A little more than a year later Jia Yi also died; at death he was thirty-three.
translations.idiomatic: A little more than a year later Jia Yi also died; he was thirty-three.

sentences.zh: ----4徙城陽王喜為淮南王。

translations.literal: ----4 King Xi of Chengyang was moved to be king of Huainan.
translations.idiomatic: ----4 King Xi of Chengyang was moved to be king of Huainan.

sentences.zh: ----5匈奴寇狄道。

translations.literal: ----5 The Xiongnu raided Didao.
translations.idiomatic: ----5 The Xiongnu raided Didao.

sentences.zh: 時匈奴數為邊患，太子家令穎川晁錯上言兵事曰：

translations.literal: At that time the Xiongnu repeatedly made border trouble; the crown prince's household intendant Chao Cuo of Yingchuan spoke on military affairs, saying:
translations.idiomatic: At that time the Xiongnu repeatedly troubled the frontier; the crown prince's household intendant Chao Cuo of Yingchuan spoke on military affairs, saying:

sentences.zh: :「《兵法》曰：『有必勝之將，無必勝之民。

translations.literal: :"The Art of War says: 'There may be a commander sure to win; there is no people sure to win.
translations.idiomatic: :"The Art of War says, 'There may be a commander sure to win; there is no people sure to win.

sentences.zh: 』由此觀之，安邊境，立功名，在於良將，不可不擇也。

translations.literal: ' From this we see that to secure the borders and establish merit and fame lies in good commanders—they cannot go unchosen.
translations.idiomatic: ' From this we see that to secure the borders and establish merit and fame lies in good commanders—they cannot go unchosen.

sentences.zh: :臣又聞，用兵臨戰合刃之急者三：一曰得地形，二曰卒服習，三曰器用利。

translations.literal: :Your servant has also heard that in employing troops, when battle is joined and blades meet, three urgencies arise: first, gaining terrain; second, soldiers trained and accustomed; third, weapons and gear sharp.
translations.idiomatic: :Your servant has also heard that in employing troops, when battle is joined and blades meet, three urgencies arise: first, gaining terrain; second, soldiers trained and accustomed; third, weapons and gear sharp.

sentences.zh: 兵法：步兵、車騎、弓弩、長戟、矛鋋、劍楯之地，各有所宜；

translations.literal: The art of war: infantry, chariots and cavalry, crossbows, long halberds, spears and daggers, swords and shields—each terrain has what suits it;
translations.idiomatic: The art of war: infantry, chariots and cavalry, crossbows, long halberds, spears and daggers, swords and shields—each terrain has what suits it;

sentences.zh: 不得其宜者，或十不當一。

translations.literal: where what suits is not obtained, perhaps ten will not equal one.
translations.idiomatic: where what suits is not obtained, perhaps ten will not equal one.

sentences.zh: 士不選練，卒不服習，起居不精，動靜不集，趨利弗及，避難不畢，前擊後解，與金鼓之指相失，此不習勒卒之過也，百不當十。

translations.literal: If soldiers are not chosen and drilled, troops not trained and accustomed, rising and resting not exact, movement and stillness not gathered, rushing profit not reached, fleeing harm not completed, striking forward then breaking apart in the rear, missing the gold-and-drum signals—this is the fault of not drilling troops; a hundred will not equal ten.
translations.idiomatic: If soldiers are not chosen and drilled, troops not trained and accustomed, rising and resting not exact, movement and stillness not gathered, rushing profit not reached, fleeing harm not completed, striking forward then breaking apart in the rear, missing the gold-and-drum signals—this is the fault of not drilling troops; a hundred will not equal ten.

sentences.zh: 兵不完利，與空手同；

translations.literal: If arms are not complete and sharp, it is the same as empty hands;
translations.idiomatic: If arms are not complete and sharp, it is the same as empty hands;

sentences.zh: 甲不堅密，與袒裼同；

translations.literal: if armor is not firm and close, it is the same as baring the torso;
translations.idiomatic: if armor is not firm and close, it is the same as baring the torso;

sentences.zh: 弩不可以及遠，與短兵同；

translations.literal: if crossbows cannot reach far, it is the same as short weapons;
translations.idiomatic: if crossbows cannot reach far, it is the same as short weapons;

sentences.zh: 射不能中，與無矢同；

translations.literal: if shooting cannot hit, it is the same as having no arrows;
translations.idiomatic: if shooting cannot hit, it is the same as having no arrows;

sentences.zh: 中不能入，與無鏃同；

translations.literal: if hitting cannot penetrate, it is the same as having no points;
translations.idiomatic: if hitting cannot penetrate, it is the same as having no points;

sentences.zh: 此將不省兵之禍也，五不當一。

translations.literal: this is the calamity of a commander who does not examine arms—five will not equal one.
translations.idiomatic: this is the calamity of a commander who does not examine arms—five will not equal one.

sentences.zh: 故《兵法》曰：『器械不利，以其卒予敵也；

translations.literal: Therefore the Art of War says: 'If gear is not sharp, you give your soldiers to the enemy;
translations.idiomatic: Therefore the Art of War says, 'If gear is not sharp, you give your soldiers to the enemy;

sentences.zh: 卒不可用，以其將予敵也；

translations.literal: if soldiers cannot be used, you give your commander to the enemy;
translations.idiomatic: if soldiers cannot be used, you give your commander to the enemy;

sentences.zh: 將不知兵，以其主予敵也；

translations.literal: if the commander does not know war, you give your lord to the enemy;
translations.idiomatic: if the commander does not know war, you give your lord to the enemy;

sentences.zh: 君不擇將，以其國予敵也。

translations.literal: if the ruler does not choose commanders, you give your state to the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: if the ruler does not choose commanders, you give your state to the enemy.

sentences.zh: 』四者，兵之至要也。

translations.literal: ' These four are the utmost essentials of war.
translations.idiomatic: ' These four are the utmost essentials of war.

sentences.zh: :臣又聞：小大異形，強弱異勢，險易異備。

translations.literal: :Your servant has also heard: small and large differ in form, strong and weak differ in momentum, difficult and easy differ in preparation.
translations.idiomatic: :Your servant has also heard: small and large differ in form, strong and weak differ in momentum, difficult and easy differ in preparation.

sentences.zh: 夫卑身以事強，小國之形也；

translations.literal: To abase the body in serving the strong is the form of a small state;
translations.idiomatic: To abase oneself in serving the strong is the form of a small state;

sentences.zh: 合小以攻大，敵國之形也；

translations.literal: to unite small states to attack a large one is the form of a rival state;
translations.idiomatic: to unite small states to attack a large one is the form of a rival state;

sentences.zh: 以蠻夷攻蠻夷，中國之形也。

translations.literal: to use barbarians to attack barbarians is the form of China.
translations.idiomatic: to use barbarians to attack barbarians is the form of China.

sentences.zh: 今匈奴地形、技藝與中國異，上下山阪，出入溪澗，中國之馬弗與也；

translations.literal: Now the Xiongnu's terrain and skills differ from China's: ascending and descending mountain slopes, entering and leaving streams and ravines—China's horses cannot match;
translations.idiomatic: Now the Xiongnu's terrain and skills differ from China's: ascending and descending mountain slopes, entering and leaving streams and ravines—China's horses cannot match;

sentences.zh: 險道傾仄，且馳且射，中國之騎弗與也；

translations.literal: on perilous roads steep and narrow, riding and shooting at once—China's horsemen cannot match;
translations.idiomatic: on perilous roads steep and narrow, riding and shooting at once—China's horsemen cannot match;

sentences.zh: 風雨罷勞，饑渴不困，中國之人弗與也；

translations.literal: in wind and rain, weary yet untroubled by hunger and thirst—China's people cannot match;
translations.idiomatic: in wind and rain, weary yet untroubled by hunger and thirst—China's people cannot match;

sentences.zh: 此匈奴之長技也。

translations.literal: these are the Xiongnu's long skills.
translations.idiomatic: these are the Xiongnu's long skills.

sentences.zh: 若夫平原、易地、輕車、突騎，則匈奴之眾易撓亂也；

translations.literal: As for plains, level ground, light chariots, and shock cavalry, then the Xiongnu masses are easily thrown into disorder;
translations.idiomatic: On plains, level ground, light chariots, and shock cavalry, the Xiongnu masses are easily thrown into disorder;

sentences.zh: 勁弩、長戟、射疏、及遠，則匈奴之弓弗能格也；

translations.literal: with strong crossbows, long halberds, loose volleys reaching far, then the Xiongnu bow cannot withstand;
translations.idiomatic: with strong crossbows, long halberds, loose volleys reaching far, the Xiongnu bow cannot withstand;

sentences.zh: 堅甲、利刃，長短相雜，游弩往來，什伍俱前，則匈奴之兵弗能當也；

translations.literal: with firm armor and sharp blades, long and short mixed, mobile crossbows coming and going, squads of ten and five advancing together, then the Xiongnu troops cannot withstand;
translations.idiomatic: with firm armor and sharp blades, long and short mixed, mobile crossbows coming and going, squads of ten and five advancing together, the Xiongnu troops cannot withstand;

sentences.zh: 材官騶發，矢道同的，則匈奴之革笥、木薦弗能支也；

translations.literal: when skilled archers spur and loose together, arrow paths on one mark, then the Xiongnu's leather quivers and wooden shields cannot bear up;
translations.idiomatic: when skilled archers spur and loose together, arrow paths on one mark, the Xiongnu's leather quivers and wooden shields cannot bear up;

sentences.zh: 下馬地斗，劍戟相接，去就相薄，則匈奴之足弗能給也；

translations.literal: dismounting to fight on foot, swords and halberds meeting, advance and retreat pressing close, then the Xiongnu's feet cannot keep pace;
translations.idiomatic: dismounting to fight on foot, swords and halberds meeting, advance and retreat pressing close, the Xiongnu's feet cannot keep pace;

sentences.zh: 此中國之長技也。

translations.literal: these are China's long skills.
translations.idiomatic: these are China's long skills.

sentences.zh: 以此觀之，匈奴之長技三，中國之長技五。

translations.literal: Viewed thus, the Xiongnu have three long skills; China has five.
translations.idiomatic: Viewed thus, the Xiongnu have three long skills; China has five.

sentences.zh: 陛下又興數十萬之眾以誅數萬之匈奴，眾寡之計，以一擊十之術也。

translations.literal: Your Majesty further raises hundreds of thousands to punish tens of thousands of Xiongnu—the calculus of many against few, the method of one striking ten.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty further raises hundreds of thousands to punish tens of thousands of Xiongnu—the calculus of many against few, the method of one striking ten.

sentences.zh: :雖然，兵，兇器；

translations.literal: :Even so, arms are baleful tools;
translations.idiomatic: :Even so, arms are baleful tools;

sentences.zh: 戰，危事也。

translations.literal: war is a perilous affair.
translations.idiomatic: war is a perilous affair.

sentences.zh: 故以大為小，以強為弱，在俛仰之間耳。

translations.literal: Therefore to turn great into small, strong into weak, lies in a bow or a rise.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore to turn great into small, strong into weak, lies in a bow or a rise.

sentences.zh: 夫以人之死爭勝，跌而不振，則悔之無及也。

translations.literal: To contend for victory with men's deaths—if one stumbles and does not recover, regret comes too late.
translations.idiomatic: To contend for victory with men's deaths—if one stumbles and does not recover, regret comes too late.

sentences.zh: 帝王之道，出於萬全。

translations.literal: The way of emperors and kings proceeds from utmost security.
translations.idiomatic: The way of emperors and kings proceeds from utmost security.

sentences.zh: 今降胡、義渠、蠻夷之屬來歸誼者，其眾數千，飲食、長技與匈奴同。

translations.literal: Now surrendered Hu, Yiqu, and barbarian sorts who come in good faith number several thousand; diet and long skills are the same as the Xiongnu's.
translations.idiomatic: Now surrendered Hu, Yiqu, and barbarian sorts who come in good faith number several thousand; diet and long skills are the same as the Xiongnu's.

sentences.zh: 可賜之堅甲、絮衣、勁弓、利矢，益以邊郡之良騎，令明將能知其習俗、和輯其心者，以陛下之明約將之。

translations.literal: They may be granted firm armor, padded garments, strong bows, and sharp arrows, increased with good cavalry of the border commanderies, and placed under clear-sighted commanders who know their customs and harmonize their hearts—under Your Majesty's bright bond to lead them.
translations.idiomatic: Grant them firm armor, padded garments, strong bows, and sharp arrows, add good cavalry from the border commanderies, and place them under clear-sighted commanders who know their customs and harmonize their hearts—under Your Majesty's bright bond to lead them.

sentences.zh: 即有險阻，以此當之；

translations.literal: Where there is rough ground, use these to meet them;
translations.idiomatic: Where there is rough ground, use these to meet them;

sentences.zh: 平地通道，則以輕車、材官制之；

translations.literal: on level ground and open roads, then use light chariots and skilled archers to control them;
translations.idiomatic: on level ground and open roads, use light chariots and skilled archers to control them;

sentences.zh: 兩軍相為表里，各用其長技，衡加之以眾，此萬全之術也。

translations.literal: the two armies acting as inner and outer, each employing its long skills, with numbers added in balance—this is the method of utmost security.
translations.idiomatic: the two armies acting as inner and outer, each employing its long skills, with numbers added in balance—this is the method of utmost security.

sentences.zh: 帝嘉之，賜錯書，寵答焉。

translations.literal: The emperor praised it, bestowed a letter on Chao Cuo, and favored him with a reply.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor praised it, bestowed a letter on Chao Cuo, and favored him with a reply.

sentences.zh: 錯又上言曰：:「臣聞秦起兵而攻胡、粵者，非以衛邊地而救民死也，貪戾而欲廣大也，故功未立而天下亂。

translations.literal: Chao Cuo again submitted, saying: :"Your servant has heard that when Qin raised troops to attack the Hu and Yue, it was not to guard the borderlands and save the people from death, but from greed and harshness wishing to expand; therefore merit was not established and all under Heaven fell into disorder.
translations.idiomatic: Chao Cuo again submitted, saying: :"Your servant has heard that when Qin raised troops to attack the Hu and Yue, it was not to guard the borderlands and save the people from death, but from greed and harshness wishing to expand; therefore merit was not established and all under Heaven fell into disorder.

sentences.zh: 且夫起兵而不知其勢，戰則為人禽，屯則卒積死。

translations.literal: Moreover, to raise troops without knowing the momentum—if you fight you become another's captive; if you encamp your soldiers pile up dead.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, to raise troops without knowing the momentum—if you fight you become another's captive; if you encamp your soldiers pile up dead.

sentences.zh: 夫胡、貉之人，其性耐寒；

translations.literal: The people of the Hu and Mo by nature endure cold;
translations.idiomatic: The people of the Hu and Mo by nature endure cold;

sentences.zh: 揚、粵之人，其性耐暑。

translations.literal: the people of Yang and Yue by nature endure heat.
translations.idiomatic: the people of Yang and Yue by nature endure heat.

sentences.zh: 秦之戍卒不耐其水土，戍者死於邊，輸者僨於道。

translations.literal: Qin's garrison soldiers could not endure their water and soil; garrison men died on the frontier, transport men collapsed on the road.
translations.idiomatic: Qin's garrison soldiers could not endure their water and soil; garrison men died on the frontier, transport men collapsed on the road.

sentences.zh: 秦民見行，如往棄市，因以謫發之，名曰『謫戍』；

translations.literal: When Qin people saw they were to go, it was like going to the execution ground; therefore they were sent by penal transport, named 'penal frontier service';
translations.idiomatic: When Qin people saw they were to go, it was like going to the execution ground; therefore they were sent by penal transport, named 'penal frontier service';

sentences.zh: 先發吏有謫及贅婿、賈人，後以嘗有市籍者，又後以大父母、父母嘗有市籍者，後入閭取其左。

translations.literal: first were sent officials with penal marks, surplus sons-in-law, and merchants; later those who had once held market registry; later those whose grandfathers and fathers had once held market registry; finally they entered the lanes and took those of the left.
translations.idiomatic: first were sent officials with penal marks, surplus sons-in-law, and merchants; later those who had once held market registry; later those whose grandfathers and fathers had once held market registry; finally they entered the lanes and took those of the left.

sentences.zh: 發之不順，行者憤怨，有萬死之害而亡銖兩之報，死事之後，不得一算之復，天下明知禍烈及己也。

translations.literal: The dispatch was not accordant; travelers were angry and resentful—ten thousand deaths' harm without a speck of reward; after dying in service they received not one tally's restitution; all under Heaven clearly knew calamity fierce would reach themselves.
translations.idiomatic: The dispatch was not accordant; travelers were angry and resentful—ten thousand deaths' harm without a speck of reward; after dying in service they received not one tally's restitution; all under Heaven clearly knew calamity fierce would reach themselves.

sentences.zh: 陳勝行戍，至於大澤，為天下先倡，天下從之如流水者，秦以威劫而行之之敝也。

translations.literal: Chen Sheng on penal frontier march reached the great marsh and was first to raise the cry under Heaven; that all under Heaven followed like flowing water was the harm of Qin's going by coercive awe.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Sheng on penal frontier march reached the great marsh and was first to raise the cry under Heaven; that all under Heaven followed like flowing water was the harm of Qin's going by coercive awe.

sentences.zh: :胡人衣食之業，不著於地，其勢易以擾亂邊境，往來轉徙，時至時去。

translations.literal: :The Hu people's livelihood of food and clothing is not fixed to the land; their momentum easily disturbs the borderlands, coming and going in shifts, arriving and departing by season.
translations.idiomatic: :The Hu people's livelihood of food and clothing is not fixed to the land; their momentum easily disturbs the borderlands, coming and going in shifts, arriving and departing by season.

sentences.zh: 此胡人之生業，而中國之所以離南□也。

translations.literal: This is the Hu people's livelihood, and why China must leave the southern □.
translations.idiomatic: This is the Hu people's livelihood, and why China must leave the southern □.

sentences.zh: 今胡人數轉牧、行獵於塞下，以候備塞之卒，卒少則入。

translations.literal: Now the Hu repeatedly shift pasture and hunt below the passes to watch the garrison troops who guard the passes; when troops are few they enter.
translations.idiomatic: Now the Hu repeatedly shift pasture and hunt below the passes to watch the garrison troops who guard the passes; when troops are few they enter.

sentences.zh: 陛下不救，則邊民絕望而有降敵之心；

translations.literal: If Your Majesty does not rescue them, border people lose hope and gain a heart to surrender to the enemy;
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty does not rescue them, border people lose hope and gain a heart to surrender to the enemy;

sentences.zh: 救之，少發則不足，多發，遠縣才至，則胡又已去。

translations.literal: if you rescue them, a small dispatch is insufficient; a large dispatch—from distant counties just arrives, and the Hu have already gone.
translations.idiomatic: if you rescue them, a small dispatch is insufficient; a large dispatch—from distant counties just arrives, and the Hu have already gone.

sentences.zh: 聚而不罷，為費甚大；

translations.literal: To gather and not dismiss costs greatly;
translations.idiomatic: To gather and not dismiss costs greatly;

sentences.zh: 罷之，則胡復入。

translations.literal: to dismiss them, and the Hu enter again.
translations.idiomatic: to dismiss them, and the Hu enter again.

sentences.zh: 如此連年，則中國貧苦而民不安矣。

translations.literal: Thus year after year, China grows poor and bitter and the people are unquiet.
translations.idiomatic: Thus year after year, China grows poor and bitter and the people are unquiet.

sentences.zh: 陛下幸憂邊境，遣將吏發卒以治塞，甚大惠也。

translations.literal: Your Majesty has been pleased to worry over the borderlands, sending generals and officials to raise soldiers and repair the passes—this is a very great grace.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty has been pleased to worry over the borderlands, sending generals and officials to raise soldiers and repair the passes—this is a very great grace.

sentences.zh: 然今遠方之卒守塞，一歲而更，不知胡人之能。

translations.literal: Yet now soldiers from distant places guard the passes, rotated every year, and do not know the Hu people's abilities.
translations.idiomatic: Yet now soldiers from distant places guard the passes, rotated every year, and do not know the Hu people's abilities.

sentences.zh: 不如選常居者家室田作，且以備之，以便為之高城深塹；

translations.literal: Better to choose permanent residents whose families farm the fields, and with them prepare defense, so as conveniently to raise high walls and deep moats for them;
translations.idiomatic: Better to choose permanent residents whose families farm the fields, and with them prepare defense, so as conveniently to raise high walls and deep moats for them;

sentences.zh: 要害之處，通川之道，調立城邑，毋下千家。

translations.literal: at strategic points and along roads through open valleys, arrange and establish walled towns, none fewer than a thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: at strategic points and along roads through open valleys, arrange and establish walled towns, none fewer than a thousand households.

sentences.zh: 先為室屋，具田器，乃募民，免罪，拜爵，復其家，予冬夏衣、稟食，能自給而止。

translations.literal: First build houses and dwellings, provide farming tools, then recruit people—exempt from punishment, invest with rank, restore their households, grant winter and summer clothing and grain rations, stopping when they can supply themselves.
translations.idiomatic: First build houses and dwellings, provide farming tools, then recruit people—exempt from punishment, invest with rank, restore their households, grant winter and summer clothing and grain rations, stopping when they can supply themselves.

sentences.zh: 塞下之民，祿利不厚，不可使久居危難之地。

translations.literal: The people below the passes have salary and profit not thick; they cannot be made to dwell long in perilous and difficult places.
translations.idiomatic: The people below the passes have salary and profit not thick; they cannot be made to dwell long in perilous and difficult places.

sentences.zh: 胡人入驅而能止其所驅者，以其半予之，縣官為贖。

translations.literal: When the Hu enter and drive off livestock, whoever can stop what they drive off—give him half; the county office redeems it.
translations.idiomatic: When the Hu enter and drive off livestock, whoever can stop what they drive off—give him half; the county office redeems it.

sentences.zh: 其民如是，則邑里相救助，赴胡不避死。

translations.literal: If the people are thus, then towns and lanes aid one another and rush against the Hu without shunning death.
translations.idiomatic: If the people are thus, then towns and lanes aid one another and rush against the Hu without shunning death.

sentences.zh: 非以德上也，欲全親戚而利其財也；

translations.literal: This is not from virtue toward superiors, but wishing to preserve kin and profit their goods;
translations.idiomatic: This is not from virtue toward superiors, but wishing to preserve kin and profit their goods;

sentences.zh: 此與東方之戍卒不習地勢而心畏胡者功相萬也。

translations.literal: this compared with eastern garrison soldiers who do not know the terrain and in heart fear the Hu is merit ten thousandfold.
translations.idiomatic: this compared with eastern garrison soldiers who do not know the terrain and in heart fear the Hu is merit ten thousandfold.

sentences.zh: 以陛下之時，徙民實邊，使遠方無屯戍之事；

translations.literal: In Your Majesty's time, move people to fill the border, so distant places have no encamped garrison affairs;
translations.idiomatic: In Your Majesty's time, move people to fill the border, so distant places have no encamped garrison affairs;

sentences.zh: 塞下之民，父子相保，無系虜之患；

translations.literal: the people below the passes, fathers and sons protecting one another, without the trouble of being bound captive;
translations.idiomatic: the people below the passes, fathers and sons protecting one another, without the trouble of being bound captive;

sentences.zh: 利施後世，名稱聖明，其與秦之行怨民，相去遠矣。

translations.literal: benefit extending to later generations, fame called sage and bright—how far this is from Qin's course of breeding resentment in the people.
translations.idiomatic: benefit extending to later generations, fame called sage and bright—how far this is from Qin's course of breeding resentment in the people.

sentences.zh: 上從其言，募民徙塞下。

translations.literal: The emperor followed his words and recruited people to move below the passes.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor followed his words and recruited people to move below the passes.

sentences.zh: 錯復言：:「陛下幸募民徙以實塞下，使屯戍之事益省，輸將之費益寡，甚大惠也。

translations.literal: Chao Cuo again spoke: :"Your Majesty has been pleased to recruit people to move and fill the area below the passes, making encamped garrison affairs ever more spared and transport and supply costs ever fewer—this is a very great grace.
translations.idiomatic: Chao Cuo again spoke: :"Your Majesty has been pleased to recruit people to move and fill the area below the passes, making encamped garrison affairs ever more spared and transport and supply costs ever fewer—this is a very great grace.

sentences.zh: 下吏誠能稱厚惠，奉明法，存恤所徙之老弱，善遇其壯士，和輯其心而勿侵刻，使先至者安樂而不思故鄉，則貧民相慕而勸往矣。

translations.literal: If lower officials can truly match this thick grace, uphold bright law, preserve and comfort the old and weak among those moved, treat their strong men well, harmonize their hearts and not encroach harshly, so that those who arrive first are secure and glad and do not think of their old home, then poor people will admire one another and be urged to go.
translations.idiomatic: If lower officials can truly match this thick grace, uphold bright law, preserve and comfort the old and weak among those moved, treat their strong men well, harmonize their hearts and not encroach harshly, so that those who arrive first are secure and glad and do not think of their old home, then poor people will admire one another and be urged to go.

sentences.zh: 臣聞古之徙民者，相其陰陽之和，嘗其水泉之味，然後營邑、立城、制里、割宅，先為築室家，置器物焉。

translations.literal: Your servant has heard that those who relocated the people in antiquity surveyed the harmony of yin and yang, tasted the flavor of the springs, and only then laid out settlements, raised cities, fixed wards, and allotted dwellings, first building houses and setting out utensils.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant has heard that in antiquity those who relocated people first surveyed the balance of yin and yang and tasted the local springs, and only then laid out settlements, raised cities, fixed wards, and allotted dwellings—building houses and furnishing them before the people arrived.

sentences.zh: 民至有所居，作有所用。

translations.literal: When the people arrived they had somewhere to dwell and something to use in work.
translations.idiomatic: When the people arrived, they had a place to live and tools to work with.

sentences.zh: 此民所以輕去故鄉而勸之新邑也。

translations.literal: This is why the people lightly left their old homeland and were encouraged toward the new settlement.
translations.idiomatic: That is why people could leave their old homeland without regret and were drawn to the new settlement.

sentences.zh: 為置醫、巫以救疾病，以修祭祀，男女有昏，生死相恤，墳墓相從，種樹畜長，室屋完安。

translations.literal: For them physicians and shamans were set up to treat illness and maintain sacrifices; men and women were married, the living and dead aided one another, graves followed in succession, trees were planted and livestock raised, and houses were made whole and secure.
translations.idiomatic: Physicians and shamans were provided to treat illness and maintain sacrifices; marriages were arranged, neighbors aided one another in life and death, families buried their dead together, trees were planted and livestock raised, and houses were kept in good repair.

sentences.zh: 此所以使民樂其處而有長居之心也。

translations.literal: This is how the people were made to delight in their place and have a mind to settle long.
translations.idiomatic: That is how people were made content where they lived and inclined to stay for good.

sentences.zh: :臣又聞古之制邊縣以備敵也，使五家為伍，伍有長；

translations.literal: :Your servant has also heard that in antiquity frontier counties were organized to guard against enemies: five households made a squad, and the squad had a leader;
translations.idiomatic: Your servant has also heard that in antiquity frontier counties were organized against the enemy: five households formed a squad, each squad with a leader;

sentences.zh: 十長一里，里有假士；

translations.literal: ten leaders made a li, and the li had an acting cadet;
translations.idiomatic: ten squad leaders formed a li, and each li had an acting cadet;

sentences.zh: 四里一連，連有假五百；

translations.literal: four li made a company, and the company had an acting commandant of five hundred;
translations.idiomatic: four li formed a company, and each company had an acting commandant of five hundred;

sentences.zh: 十連一邑，邑有假候。

translations.literal: ten companies made a town, and the town had an acting frontier marquis.
translations.idiomatic: ten companies formed a town, and each town had an acting frontier marquis.

sentences.zh: 皆擇其邑之賢材有護、習地形、知民心者。

translations.literal: In each case they chose from the town's worthy talents those who were protective, versed in the terrain, and knew the people's hearts.
translations.idiomatic: In every case they chose men of talent in the town who were protective, knew the terrain, and understood the people's hearts.

sentences.zh: 居則習民於射法，出則教民於應敵。

translations.literal: At rest they drilled the people in archery; abroad they taught the people how to meet the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: In peacetime they drilled the people in archery; in campaign they taught them how to face the enemy.

sentences.zh: 故卒伍成於內，則軍政定於外。

translations.literal: Thus when squads and companies were formed within, military affairs were settled without.
translations.idiomatic: Thus when squads and companies were formed at home, military order was secure abroad.

sentences.zh: 服習以成，勿令遷徙，幼則同游，長則共事。

translations.literal: Through practice they were made accomplished; they were not allowed to move away—children played together, adults worked together.
translations.idiomatic: Through long practice they became skilled; they were not allowed to move away—children grew up together, adults served together.

sentences.zh: 夜戰聲相知，則足以相救；

translations.literal: In night battle their voices knew one another, and that was enough to rescue one another;
translations.idiomatic: In night battle they knew one another's voices and could rescue one another;

sentences.zh: 晝戰目相見，則足以相識；

translations.literal: in day battle their eyes saw one another, and that was enough to recognize one another;
translations.idiomatic: in day battle they saw one another's faces and could recognize one another;

sentences.zh: 歡愛之心，足以相死。

translations.literal: the heart of affection was enough to die for one another.
translations.idiomatic: their bonds of affection were enough to make them die for one another.

sentences.zh: 如此而勸以厚賞，威以重罰，則前死不還踵矣。

translations.literal: With this, if encouraged by rich rewards and awed by heavy punishments, they would die forward without turning the heel.
translations.idiomatic: Encouraged with rich rewards and awed with heavy punishments, men so bound would die forward without turning back.

sentences.zh: 所徙之民非壯有材者，但費衣糧，不可用也；

translations.literal: If those relocated were not strong men of talent, they only wasted clothing and grain and could not be used;
translations.idiomatic: If those relocated were not able-bodied men of talent, they only wasted clothing and grain and were of no use;

sentences.zh: 雖有材力，不得良吏，猶亡功也。

translations.literal: even if they had strength and ability, without good officials there would still be no achievement.
translations.idiomatic: even with strength and ability, without good officials there would still be no success.

sentences.zh: :陛下絕匈奴不與和親，臣竊意其冬來南也；

translations.literal: :Your Majesty has cut off the Xiongnu and granted no marriage-alliance; your servant ventures to suppose they will come south in winter;
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty has broken with the Xiongnu and refused marriage-alliance; your servant ventures to suppose they will come south in winter;

sentences.zh: 壹大治，則終身創矣。

translations.literal: one great punitive campaign, and they will bear a lifelong wound.
translations.idiomatic: one great campaign, and they will suffer a wound for life.

sentences.zh: 欲立威者，始於折膠；

translations.literal: One who wishes to establish awe must begin when the glue freezes;
translations.idiomatic: He who would establish awe must strike when the glue freezes;

sentences.zh: 來而不能困，使得氣去，後未易服也。

translations.literal: if they come yet cannot be trapped and are allowed to depart in high spirits, afterward they will not be easy to subdue.
translations.idiomatic: if they come yet cannot be trapped and are allowed to withdraw in high spirits, they will not be easy to subdue afterward.

sentences.zh: 錯為人峭直刻深，以其辯得幸太子，太子家號曰「智囊」。

translations.literal: Chao Cuo as a man was stern, upright, and severe; by his eloquence he won favor with the crown prince, and the prince's household called him the "Wisdom Satchel."
translations.idiomatic: Chao Cuo was stern, upright, and severe; by his eloquence he won favor with the crown prince, and the prince's household called him the "Wisdom Satchel."

sentences.zh: ----1冬，十二月，河決酸棗，東潰金堤、東郡；

translations.literal: ----1 In winter, the twelfth month, the Yellow River burst its banks at Suanzao and breached eastward through the Golden Dike into Dong commandery;
translations.idiomatic: ----1 In winter, the twelfth month, the Yellow River burst at Suanzao and breached eastward through the Golden Dike into Dong commandery;

sentences.zh: 大興卒塞之。

translations.literal: corvée labor was raised on a great scale to block it.
translations.idiomatic: corvée labor was raised on a great scale to block the breach.

sentences.zh: ----2春，三月，除關，無用傳。

translations.literal: ----2 In spring, the third month, the passes were abolished and travel documents were no longer required.
translations.idiomatic: ----2 In spring, the third month, the passes were abolished and travel documents were no longer required.

sentences.zh: ----3晁錯言於上曰：

translations.literal: ----3 Chao Cuo spoke to the emperor, saying:
translations.idiomatic: ----3 Chao Cuo spoke to the emperor, saying:

sentences.zh: :「聖王在上而民不凍饑者，非能耕而食之，織而衣之也，為開其資財之道也。

translations.literal: :"When a sage king is above and the people are not cold or hungry, it is not that he can plow and feed them or weave and clothe them—he opens the ways by which they may gain wealth and goods.
translations.idiomatic: "When a sage king reigns and the people are neither cold nor hungry, it is not because he plows and feeds them or weaves and clothes them—he opens the ways by which they may gain wealth."

sentences.zh: 故堯有九年之水，湯有七年之旱，而國亡捐瘠者，以畜積多而備先具也。

translations.literal: Thus when Yao had nine years of flood and Tang seven years of drought, the state had none who died emaciated, because stores were many and preparations were made beforehand.
translations.idiomatic: When Yao had nine years of flood and Tang seven years of drought, no one in the state died of starvation, because stores were ample and preparations had been made in advance.

sentences.zh: 今海內為一，土地、人民之眾不減湯、禹，加以無天災數年之水旱，而畜積未及者，何也？

translations.literal: Now within the seas all is one; land and people are no fewer than under Tang and Yu; moreover there have been no heaven-sent disasters of flood or drought for several years—yet stores have not reached that level. Why?
translations.idiomatic: Now the realm is united; land and people are no fewer than under Tang and Yu; and for several years there have been no heaven-sent floods or droughts—yet stores have not reached that level. Why?

sentences.zh: 地有遺利，民有餘力；

translations.literal: The land has profit left unused, and the people have strength left over;
translations.idiomatic: The land still holds unused profit, and the people still have strength to spare;

sentences.zh: 生谷之土未盡墾，山澤之利未盡出，游食之民未盡歸農也。

translations.literal: soil that can bear grain is not fully opened, the profit of mountains and marshes is not fully drawn forth, and roaming eaters have not all returned to farming.
translations.idiomatic: land that can bear grain is not fully opened, the profit of mountains and marshes is not fully drawn forth, and roaming eaters have not all returned to farming.

sentences.zh: :夫寒之於衣，不待輕暖；

translations.literal: :As to cold toward clothing, one does not wait for light warmth;
translations.idiomatic: As for cold, one does not wait for light garments;

sentences.zh: 饑之於食，不待甘旨；

translations.literal: as to hunger toward food, one does not wait for sweet delicacies;
translations.idiomatic: as for hunger, one does not wait for fine delicacies;

sentences.zh: 饑寒至身，不顧廉恥。

translations.literal: when hunger and cold reach the person, one does not regard integrity and shame.
translations.idiomatic: when hunger and cold reach the body, integrity and shame are forgotten.

sentences.zh: 人情，一日不再食則饑，終歲不製衣則寒。

translations.literal: Human feeling is such: one day without eating again brings hunger; a whole year without making clothes brings cold.
translations.idiomatic: Human nature is such: one day without a second meal brings hunger; a whole year without new clothes brings cold.

sentences.zh: 夫腹饑不得食，膚寒不得衣，雖慈母不能保其子，君安能以有其民哉！

translations.literal: When the belly is hungry yet cannot obtain food, when the skin is cold yet cannot obtain clothing—even a loving mother cannot preserve her child; how can a lord thereby possess his people!
translations.idiomatic: When the belly is hungry yet there is no food, when the skin is cold yet there is no clothing—even a loving mother cannot save her child; how then can a ruler hold his people!

sentences.zh: 明主知其然也，故務民於農桑，薄賦斂，廣畜積，以實倉廩，備水旱，故民可得而有也。

translations.literal: An enlightened ruler knows this and therefore sets the people to farming and sericulture, lightens taxes and levies, broadens stores, fills the granaries, and prepares against flood and drought—thus the people can be obtained and held.
translations.idiomatic: An enlightened ruler knows this and therefore sets the people to farming and sericulture, lightens taxes, broadens stores, fills the granaries, and prepares against flood and drought—thus the people can be held.

sentences.zh: 民者，在上所以牧之；

translations.literal: The people are what those above shepherd;
translations.idiomatic: The people are what those above shepherd;

sentences.zh: 民之趨利，如水走下，四方無擇也。

translations.literal: the people's rushing toward profit is like water running downhill—there is no choosing among the four directions.
translations.idiomatic: the people's rush toward profit is like water running downhill—they choose no direction.

sentences.zh: :夫珠、玉、金、銀，饑不可食，寒不可衣；

translations.literal: :Pearls, jade, gold, and silver—hungry, one cannot eat them; cold, one cannot wear them;
translations.idiomatic: Pearls, jade, gold, and silver—when hungry one cannot eat them; when cold one cannot wear them;

sentences.zh: 然而眾貴之者，以上用之故也。

translations.literal: yet the multitude values them because those above use them.
translations.idiomatic: yet the multitude values them because those above use them.

sentences.zh: 其為物輕微易藏，在於把握，可以周海內而無饑寒之患。

translations.literal: As objects they are light and small, easy to hide, held in the palm, and can circle within the seas without the trouble of hunger or cold.
translations.idiomatic: They are light and small, easy to hide, held in the palm, and can be carried across the realm without fear of hunger or cold.

sentences.zh: 此令臣輕背其主，而民易去其鄉，盜賊有所勸，亡逃者得輕資也。

translations.literal: This makes ministers lightly turn from their lord and the people easily leave their villages; thieves have something to encourage them, and fugitives obtain light assets.
translations.idiomatic: This makes ministers lightly desert their lord and the people easily leave their villages; thieves are encouraged, and fugitives obtain portable wealth.

sentences.zh: 粟、米、布、帛，生於地，長於時，聚於力，非可一日成也；

translations.literal: Grain, rice, cloth, and silk are born from the earth, grow through seasons, and are gathered by labor—they cannot be completed in a day;
translations.idiomatic: Grain, rice, cloth, and silk are born from the earth, grow through the seasons, and are gathered by labor—they cannot be produced in a day;

sentences.zh: 數石之重，中人弗勝，不為奸邪所利，一日弗得而饑寒至。

translations.literal: several piculs in weight—a middling man cannot bear them; villains do not profit by them; one day without them and hunger and cold arrive.
translations.idiomatic: they weigh several piculs, which a middling man cannot carry; villains do not covet them; one day without them and hunger and cold arrive.

sentences.zh: 是故明君貴五穀而賤金玉。

translations.literal: Therefore the enlightened ruler values the five grains and holds cheap gold and jade.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore the enlightened ruler values the five grains and holds gold and jade cheap.

sentences.zh: :今農夫五口之家，其服役者不下二人，其能耕者不過百□，百□之收不過百石。

translations.literal: :Now a farming household of five mouths has no fewer than two men on corvée; those able to plow can manage no more than a hundred □, and a hundred □ in harvest yields no more than a hundred piculs.
translations.idiomatic: Now a farming household of five mouths has at least two men on corvée; those able to plow can manage no more than a hundred □, and a hundred □ yields no more than a hundred piculs.

sentences.zh: 春耕，夏耘，秋獲，冬藏，伐薪樵，治官府，給繇役；

translations.literal: In spring they plow, in summer weed, in autumn reap, in winter store; they cut firewood, attend to government offices, and supply corvée;
translations.idiomatic: In spring they plow, in summer weed, in autumn reap, in winter store; they cut firewood, attend government offices, and supply corvée;

sentences.zh: 春不得避風塵，夏不得避暑熱，秋不得避陰雨，冬不得避寒凍，四時之間亡日休息；

translations.literal: in spring they cannot avoid wind and dust, in summer heat, in autumn rain, in winter cold—between the four seasons there is no day of rest;
translations.idiomatic: in spring they cannot escape wind and dust, in summer heat, in autumn rain, in winter cold—between the four seasons there is no day of rest;

sentences.zh: 又私自送往迎來、吊死問疾、養孤長幼在其中。

translations.literal: moreover on their own they go to send off and welcome back, mourn the dead and inquire after the ill, and rear orphans and nurture the young—all within this.
translations.idiomatic: moreover on their own they send off and welcome guests, mourn the dead and inquire after the ill, and rear orphans and nurture the young—all within this.

sentences.zh: 勤苦如此，尚復被水旱之災，急政暴賦，賦斂不時，朝令而暮改。

translations.literal: Toiling so, they still suffer flood and drought, harsh government and violent levies, collections not in season, and orders changed from morning to evening.
translations.idiomatic: Toiling so, they still suffer flood and drought, harsh government and violent levies, collections out of season, and orders changed from morning to evening.

sentences.zh: 有者半賈而賣，無者取倍稱之息，於是有賣田宅、鬻子孫以償責者矣。

translations.literal: Those with goods sold at half price; those without took interest at double the principal—thus there were those who sold fields and houses or sold sons and grandsons to pay debts.
translations.idiomatic: Those with goods sold at half price; those without borrowed at double interest—thus some sold fields and houses or even sold sons and grandsons to pay debts.

sentences.zh: 而商賈大者積貯倍息，小者坐列販賣，操其奇贏，日游都市，乘上之急，所賣必倍。

translations.literal: Yet great merchants hoarded for double interest; small ones sat in rows to sell, grasping extraordinary profits, roaming the markets daily, and riding the ruler's urgency—the goods they sold were sure to double.
translations.idiomatic: Yet great merchants hoarded for double profit; small ones sat in rows to sell, grasping extraordinary gains, roaming the markets daily, and riding the ruler's urgency—whatever they sold was sure to double in price.

sentences.zh: 故其男不耕耘，女不蠶織，衣必文采，食必粱肉；

translations.literal: Thus their men did not plow, their women did not rear silkworms and weave; clothing was surely patterned brocade, food surely fine grain and meat;
translations.idiomatic: Thus their men did not plow, their women did not rear silkworms and weave; their clothing was brocade, their food fine grain and meat;

sentences.zh: 無農夫之苦，有仟伯之得。

translations.literal: without the farmer's toil, they had gains of a thousand per hundred.
translations.idiomatic: without the farmer's toil, they had gains in the thousands.

sentences.zh: 因其富厚，交通王侯，力過吏勢，以利相傾；

translations.literal: Relying on their wealth and substance, they connected with kings and marquises, their power surpassing officials' authority, overthrowing one another for profit;
translations.idiomatic: Relying on their wealth, they cultivated ties with kings and marquises, their power surpassing officials', and overthrew rivals for profit;

sentences.zh: 千里游敖，冠蓋相望，乘堅、策肥，履絲、曳縞。

translations.literal: they roamed and played a thousand li; caps and carriage covers looked upon one another; they rode sturdy carts and drove fat horses, wore silk and trailed white gauze.
translations.idiomatic: they roamed a thousand li; caps and carriage covers filled the roads; they rode sturdy carts and drove fat horses, wore silk and trailed white gauze.

sentences.zh: 此商人所以兼併農人，農人所以流亡者也。

translations.literal: This is why merchants annex farmers and farmers go into exile.
translations.idiomatic: This is why merchants annex farmers and farmers flee their fields.

sentences.zh: :方今之務，莫若使民務農而已矣。

translations.literal: :Of present tasks, nothing is better than simply making the people attend to farming.
translations.idiomatic: Of present tasks, nothing is better than making the people attend to farming.

sentences.zh: 欲民務農，在於貴粟。

translations.literal: To make the people attend to farming lies in valuing grain.
translations.idiomatic: To make the people attend to farming lies in valuing grain.

sentences.zh: 貴粟之道，在於使民以粟為賞罰。

translations.literal: The way to value grain lies in making the people use grain for rewards and punishments.
translations.idiomatic: The way to value grain lies in making the people use grain for rewards and punishments.

sentences.zh: 今募天下入粟縣官，得以拜爵，得以除罪。

translations.literal: Now summon all under Heaven to present grain to the government granaries: they may thereby receive rank and may thereby expiate crime.
translations.idiomatic: Now summon all under Heaven to present grain to the government granaries: they may receive rank and may expiate crime.

sentences.zh: 如此，富人有爵，農民有錢，粟有所渫。

translations.literal: Thus the rich have rank, farmers have money, and grain has somewhere to drain.
translations.idiomatic: Thus the rich gain rank, farmers gain money, and grain is dispersed where needed.

sentences.zh: 夫能入粟以受爵，皆有餘者也。

translations.literal: Those able to present grain to receive rank are all men of surplus.
translations.idiomatic: Those able to present grain for rank are all men of surplus.

sentences.zh: 取於有餘以供上用，則貧民之賦可損，所謂損有餘，補不足，令出而民利者也。

translations.literal: Taking from surplus to supply the ruler's use, the poor people's levies can be reduced—this is what is called reducing surplus and supplementing insufficiency: orders go forth and the people profit.
translations.idiomatic: Taking from surplus to supply the ruler's use, the poor people's levies can be reduced—this is reducing surplus to supplement insufficiency: orders go forth and the people profit.

sentences.zh: 今令民有車騎馬一匹者，復卒三人；

translations.literal: Now the order is: if a man has one war-horse for chariot and cavalry, three corvée laborers are exempted;
translations.idiomatic: Now the order is: if a man presents one war-horse for chariot and cavalry, three corvée laborers are exempted;

sentences.zh: 車騎者，天下武備也，故為復卒。

translations.literal: chariots and cavalry are the realm's military equipment, and therefore corvée is exempted.
translations.idiomatic: chariots and cavalry are the realm's military equipment, and therefore corvée is exempted.

sentences.zh: 神農之教曰：『有石城十仞，湯池百步，帶甲百萬，而無粟，弗能守也。

translations.literal: The teaching of Shennong says: 'Though there be stone walls ten ren high, boiling moats a hundred paces wide, and a million armored men, without grain they cannot be held.
translations.idiomatic: The teaching of Shennong says, 'Though there be stone walls ten ren high, boiling moats a hundred paces wide, and a million armored men, without grain they cannot be held.

sentences.zh: 』以是觀之，粟者，王者大用，政之本務。

translations.literal: ' Viewed thus, grain is the great instrument of a king, the root task of government.
translations.idiomatic: ' Viewed thus, grain is the great instrument of a king and the root task of government.

sentences.zh: 令民入粟受爵至五大夫以上，乃復一人耳，此其與騎馬之功相去遠矣。

translations.literal: To make the people present grain for rank up to the fifth grandee and above exempts only one man—how far this is from the merit of presenting a cavalry horse!
translations.idiomatic: To make the people present grain for rank up to the fifth grandee and above exempts only one man—how far this falls short of the merit of presenting a cavalry horse!

sentences.zh: 爵者，上之所擅，出於口而無窮；

translations.literal: Rank is what those above monopolize—it comes from the mouth and is without limit;
translations.idiomatic: Rank is what those above monopolize—it comes from the mouth and is without limit;

sentences.zh: 粟者，民之所種，生於地而不乏。

translations.literal: grain is what the people plant—it grows from the earth and is not exhausted.
translations.idiomatic: grain is what the people plant—it grows from the earth and is not exhausted.

sentences.zh: 夫得高爵與免罪，人之所甚欲也；

translations.literal: To obtain high rank and exemption from punishment is what people most desire;
translations.idiomatic: High rank and exemption from punishment are what people most desire;

sentences.zh: 使天下人入粟於邊以受爵、免罪，不過三歲，塞下之粟必多矣。

translations.literal: if all under Heaven present grain at the frontier to receive rank and expiate crime, within no more than three years the grain below the passes will surely be abundant.
translations.idiomatic: if all under Heaven present grain at the frontier for rank and to expiate crime, within three years the grain below the passes will surely be abundant.

sentences.zh: 帝從之，令民入粟邊，拜爵各以多少級數為差。

translations.literal: The emperor followed this and ordered the people to present grain at the frontier; enfeoffment in rank differed according to how many grades were presented.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor followed this and ordered the people to present grain at the frontier; rank was granted in proportion to the amount presented.

sentences.zh: 錯復奏言：「陛下幸使天下入粟塞下以拜爵，甚大惠也。

translations.literal: Chao Cuo again memorialized, saying: "Your Majesty has graciously had all under Heaven present grain below the passes to receive rank—a very great favor.
translations.idiomatic: Chao Cuo again memorialized, saying, "Your Majesty has graciously had all under Heaven present grain below the passes to receive rank—a very great favor.

sentences.zh: 竊恐塞卒之食不足用，大渫天下粟。

translations.literal: Your servant fears the frontier soldiers' food may not suffice; greatly drain the realm's grain.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant fears the frontier soldiers' food may not suffice and urges a great draining of grain throughout the realm.

sentences.zh: 邊食足以支五歲，可令入粟郡縣矣；

translations.literal: When frontier stores suffice for five years, the people may be ordered to present grain to commanderies and counties;
translations.idiomatic: When frontier stores suffice for five years, the people may be ordered to present grain to commanderies and counties;

sentences.zh: 郡縣足支一歲以上，可時赦，勿收農民租。

translations.literal: when commanderies and counties suffice for more than a year, amnesties may be timed and farmers' rents not collected.
translations.idiomatic: when commanderies and counties suffice for more than a year, amnesties may be granted and farmers' rents waived.

sentences.zh: 如此，德澤加於萬民，民愈勤農，大富樂矣。

translations.literal: Thus benevolence and favor would reach the myriad people, the people would be all the more diligent in farming, and there would be great wealth and joy.
translations.idiomatic: Thus favor would reach the myriad people, the people would be all the more diligent in farming, and there would be great wealth and joy.

sentences.zh: 上復從其言，詔曰：「道民之路，在於務本。

translations.literal: The emperor again followed his words and issued an edict, saying: "The way to lead the people lies in attending to the root.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor again followed his words and issued an edict, saying, "The way to lead the people lies in attending to the root.

sentences.zh: 朕親率天下農，十年於今，而野不加辟，歲一不登，民有饑色；

translations.literal: I have personally led all under Heaven in farming for ten years until now, yet the wilds are not further opened; one year of poor harvest and the people show the color of hunger;
translations.idiomatic: I have personally led all under Heaven in farming for ten years until now, yet the wilds are not further opened; one poor harvest and the people show hunger in their faces;

sentences.zh: 是從事焉尚寡而吏未加務。

translations.literal: this shows that those engaged in it are still few and officials have not increased their exertions.
translations.idiomatic: this shows that too few are engaged in it and officials have not increased their exertions.

sentences.zh: 吾詔書數下，歲勸民種樹而功未興，是吏奉吾詔不勤而勸民不明也。

translations.literal: My edicts have gone down repeatedly, and each year the people are urged to plant trees yet the work has not flourished—this is because officials do not diligently carry out my edicts and do not clearly urge the people.
translations.idiomatic: My edicts have gone down repeatedly, and each year the people are urged to plant trees yet the work has not flourished—this is because officials do not diligently carry out my edicts and do not clearly urge the people.

sentences.zh: 且吾農民甚苦而吏莫之省，將何以功焉！

translations.literal: Moreover my farmers are very bitterly toiling yet officials do not look into it for them—how shall achievement be made!
translations.idiomatic: Moreover my farmers toil bitterly yet officials do not look into it—how shall achievement be made!

sentences.zh: 其賜農民今年租稅之半。

translations.literal: Let half this year's rent and tax be granted to farmers.
translations.idiomatic: Let half this year's rent and tax be granted to farmers.

sentences.zh: 」----1春，二月，甲寅，詔日；

translations.literal: " ----1 In spring, the second month, on jiayin, an edict day;
translations.idiomatic: " ----1 In spring, the second month, on jiayin, an edict said:

sentences.zh: 「朕親率天下農耕以供粢盛，皇后親桑以供祭服；

translations.literal: "I shall personally lead all under Heaven in plowing and sowing to supply the sacrificial grain vessels; the empress shall personally tend silkworms to supply sacrificial robes;
translations.idiomatic: "I shall personally lead all under Heaven in plowing and sowing to supply the sacrificial grain vessels; the empress shall personally tend silkworms to supply sacrificial robes;

sentences.zh: 其具禮儀。

translations.literal: let the full rites be prepared."
translations.idiomatic: let the full rites be prepared."

sentences.zh: 」----2初，秦時祝官有祕祝，即有災祥，輒移過於下。

translations.literal: " ----2 At the outset, in Qin times the prayer officials had secret invocations: whenever there was disaster or omen, blame was at once shifted downward.
translations.idiomatic: " ----2 At the outset, in Qin times the prayer officials had secret invocations: whenever there was disaster or omen, blame was at once shifted downward.

sentences.zh: 夏，詔曰：「蓋聞天道，禍自怨起而福繇德興，百官之非，宜由朕躬。

translations.literal: In summer, an edict said: "I have heard that the Way of Heaven is such: disaster arises from resentment and blessing follows virtue; the faults of the hundred officials ought to rest on my person.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, an edict said, "I have heard that the Way of Heaven is such: disaster arises from resentment and blessing follows virtue; the faults of the hundred officials ought to rest on my person.

sentences.zh: 今祕祝之官移過於下，以彰吾之不德，朕甚弗取。

translations.literal: Now the secret-invocation officials shift blame downward to display my want of virtue—this I very much do not accept.
translations.idiomatic: Now the secret-invocation officials shift blame downward to display my want of virtue—this I very much do not accept.

sentences.zh: 其除之！

translations.literal: Let them be abolished!"
translations.idiomatic: Let them be abolished!"

sentences.zh: 」----3齊太倉令淳于意有罪，當刑，詔獄逮系長安。

translations.literal: " ----3 Chunyu Yi, Grand Granary Master of Qi, was guilty and due for punishment; the edict prison arrested and held him in Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: " ----3 Chunyu Yi, Grand Granary Master of Qi, was guilty and due for punishment; the edict prison arrested and held him in Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 其少女緹縈上書曰：「妾父為吏，齊中皆稱其廉平；

translations.literal: His young daughter Ti Ying submitted a memorial, saying: "Your handmaid's father served as an official, and throughout Qi all called him incorrupt and fair;
translations.idiomatic: His young daughter Ti Ying submitted a memorial, saying, "Your handmaid's father served as an official, and throughout Qi all called him incorrupt and fair;

sentences.zh: 今坐法當刑。

translations.literal: now, convicted by law, he is due for punishment.
translations.idiomatic: now, convicted by law, he is due for punishment.

sentences.zh: 妾傷夫死者不可復生，刑者不可復屬，雖後欲改過自新，其道無繇也。

translations.literal: Your handmaid grieves that one who has died cannot live again, that one who has been mutilated cannot be made whole again—even if afterward he wished to reform and renew himself, there would be no way.
translations.idiomatic: Your handmaid grieves that the dead cannot live again, that the mutilated cannot be made whole again—even if afterward he wished to reform and renew himself, there would be no way.

sentences.zh: 妾願沒入為官婢，以贖父刑罪，使得自新。

translations.literal: Your handmaid wishes to be confiscated and made a government bondwoman to redeem her father's punishment, so that he may renew himself.
translations.idiomatic: Your handmaid wishes to be confiscated and made a government bondwoman to redeem her father's punishment, so that he may have a chance to reform.

sentences.zh: 天子憐悲其意，五月，詔曰：「《詩》曰：『愷弟君子，民之父母。

translations.literal: The Son of Heaven pitied and grieved their intent; in the fifth month an edict said: "The Odes says: 'A genial, younger-brother-like gentleman is the people's parent.
translations.idiomatic: The Son of Heaven pitied and grieved their plight; in the fifth month an edict said: "The Odes says: 'A genial, younger-brother-like gentleman is the people's parent.

sentences.zh: 』今人有過，教未施而刑已加焉，或欲改行為善而道無繇至，朕甚憐之！

translations.literal: ' Now when people have faults, instruction has not been applied yet punishment is already added, or they wish to change conduct and do good yet the Way has no path to reach them—I am deeply grieved!
translations.idiomatic: ' Now when people err, instruction has not yet been applied yet punishment is already imposed, or they wish to reform and do good yet have no means to reach the Way—I am deeply grieved!

sentences.zh: 夫刑至斷支體，刻肌膚，終身不息，何其刑之痛而不德也！

translations.literal: For punishments to reach cutting off limbs and carving flesh and skin, never ceasing through life—how painful the punishment and how lacking in virtue!
translations.idiomatic: For punishments to reach cutting off limbs and carving flesh and skin, never ceasing through life—how painful the punishment and how lacking in virtue!

sentences.zh: 豈為民父母之意哉！

translations.literal: How is this the intent of being the people's parent!
translations.idiomatic: How is this the intent of being the people's parent!

sentences.zh: 其除肉刑，有以易之；

translations.literal: Abolish the mutilation punishments and have something to replace them;
translations.idiomatic: Abolish the mutilation punishments and have something to replace them;

sentences.zh: 及令罪人各以輕重，不記逃，有年而免。

translations.literal: and order that culprits each according to light and heavy [offenses], not recording flight, after a set number of years be released.
translations.idiomatic: and order that offenders each according to the severity of their crimes, without recording flight, be released after a set term of years.

sentences.zh: 具為令！

translations.literal: Draw up the statutes in full!
translations.idiomatic: Draw up the statutes in full!

sentences.zh: 丞相張蒼、御史大夫馮敬奏請定律曰：「諸當髡者為城旦、舂；

translations.literal: Chancellor Zhang Cang and Grand Secretary Feng Jing memorialized requesting fixed laws, saying: "All who ought to be shaved shall become wall-guard dawn [laborers] and pounders;
translations.idiomatic: Chancellor Zhang Cang and Grand Secretary Feng Jing memorialized requesting fixed laws, saying: "All who ought to be shaved shall become wall-guard dawn laborers and grain-pounders;

sentences.zh: 當黥者髡鉗為城旦、舂；

translations.literal: those who ought to be tattooed shall be shaved, collared, and made wall-guard dawn and pounders;
translations.idiomatic: those who ought to be tattooed shall be shaved, collared, and made wall-guard dawn laborers and grain-pounders;

sentences.zh: 當劓者笞三百；

translations.literal: those who ought to have the nose cut shall be beaten three hundred [strokes];
translations.idiomatic: those who ought to have the nose cut shall be beaten three hundred strokes;

sentences.zh: 當斬左止者笞五百；

translations.literal: those who ought to have the left foot cut off shall be beaten five hundred;
translations.idiomatic: those who ought to have the left foot cut off shall be beaten five hundred;

sentences.zh: 當斬右止及殺人先自告及吏坐受賕、枉法、守縣官財物而即盜之、已論而復有笞罪皆棄市。

translations.literal: those who ought to have the right foot cut off, and murderers who first confess themselves, and officers guilty of receiving bribes, perverting law, guarding county officials' goods yet immediately stealing them, and those already sentenced who again have beating offenses—all shall be abandoned in the market.
translations.idiomatic: those who ought to have the right foot cut off, and murderers who confess first, and officers guilty of taking bribes, perverting the law, guarding county officials' goods yet immediately stealing them, and those already sentenced who again incur beating offenses—all shall be executed in the market.

sentences.zh: 罪人獄已決為城旦、舂者，各有歲數以免。

translations.literal: Culprits whose prison cases are already decided as wall-guard dawn and pounders each have a number of years for release.
translations.idiomatic: Offenders whose prison sentences are already decided as wall-guard dawn laborers and grain-pounders each have a set term of years for release.

sentences.zh: 」制曰：「可。

translations.literal: " The rescript said: "Approved.
translations.idiomatic: " The rescript said: "Approved.

sentences.zh: 是時，上既躬修玄默，而將相皆舊功臣，少文多質。

translations.literal: At this time the Emperor had personally cultivated dark silence, while generals and chancellors were all old merit officials—little literary culture, much substance.
translations.idiomatic: At this time the Emperor had personally cultivated quiet restraint, while generals and chancellors were all old merit officials—little literary polish, much plain substance.

sentences.zh: 懲惡亡秦之政，論議務在寬厚，恥言人之過失，化行天下，告訐之俗易。

translations.literal: Chastising the evil government of perished Qin, discussion and deliberation strove to be generous and thick, ashamed to speak of people's faults; transformation spread through all under Heaven and the custom of informing was changed.
translations.idiomatic: Chastising the evil government of fallen Qin, discussion strove to be generous and mild, ashamed to speak of people's faults; transformation spread through the realm and the custom of informing was changed.

sentences.zh: 吏安其官，民樂其業，畜積歲增，戶口浸息。

translations.literal: Officers were secure in their posts, the people delighted in their occupations; livestock and stores increased year by year, households gradually grew.
translations.idiomatic: Officers were secure in their posts, the people delighted in their occupations; livestock and stores increased year by year, and households gradually multiplied.

sentences.zh: 風流篤厚，禁罔疏闊，罪疑者予民，是以刑罰大省，至於斷獄四百，有刑錯之風焉。

translations.literal: Customs were sincere and thick, prohibitions and nets sparse and broad; where guilt was doubtful the benefit went to the people—therefore punishments were greatly reduced, reaching as few as four hundred cases decided, and there was a wind of punishments misplaced.
translations.idiomatic: Customs were sincere and generous, prohibitions sparse and broad; where guilt was doubtful the benefit went to the people—therefore punishments were greatly reduced, with as few as four hundred cases decided, and there was a wind of punishments falling into disuse.

sentences.zh: ----4六月，詔曰：「農，天下之本，務莫大焉。

translations.literal: ----4 In the sixth month an edict said: "Agriculture is the root of all under Heaven; no task is greater.
translations.idiomatic: ----4 In the sixth month an edict said: "Agriculture is the root of the realm; no task is greater.

sentences.zh: 今勤身從事而有租稅之賦，是為本末者無以異也，其於勸農之道未備。

translations.literal: Now those who diligently work the fields yet have rent and tax levies—for root and branch there is no distinction; the Way of encouraging agriculture is not yet complete.
translations.idiomatic: Now those who diligently work the fields yet pay rent and tax levies—for root and branch there is no distinction; the policy of encouraging agriculture is not yet complete.

sentences.zh: 其除田之租稅。

translations.literal: Abolish the field's rent and taxes.
translations.idiomatic: Abolish the field rent and taxes.

sentences.zh: 」----1冬，匈奴老上單于十四萬騎入朝那、蕭關，殺北地都尉卬，虜人民畜產甚多；

translations.literal: " ----1 In winter the Xiongnu Laoshang Chanyu with one hundred forty thousand horsemen entered Chaona and Xiaoguan, killed Beidi Commandant Ang, and captured very many people, livestock, and goods;
translations.idiomatic: " ----1 In winter the Xiongnu Laoshang Chanyu with one hundred forty thousand horsemen entered Chaona and Xiaoguan, killed Beidi Commandant Ang, and captured very many people, livestock, and goods;

sentences.zh: 遂至彭陽，使奇兵入燒回中宮，候騎至雍甘泉。

translations.literal: he thereupon reached Pengyang, sent irregular troops in to burn the Huizhong Palace, and scout horsemen reached Yong and Ganquan.
translations.idiomatic: he thereupon reached Pengyang, sent irregular troops in to burn the Huizhong Palace, and scout horsemen reached Yong and Ganquan.

sentences.zh: 帝以中尉周舍、郎中令張武為將軍，發車千乘、騎卒十萬軍長安旁，以備胡寇；

translations.literal: The Emperor made Central Commandant Zhou She and Palace Commandant Zhang Wu generals, mobilized a thousand chariots and one hundred thousand cavalry and infantry to encamp beside Chang'an to guard against Hu bandits;
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor made Central Commandant Zhou She and Palace Commandant Zhang Wu generals, mobilized a thousand chariots and one hundred thousand cavalry and infantry to encamp beside Chang'an against Xiongnu raids;

sentences.zh: 而拜昌侯盧卿為上郡將軍，甯侯魏□為北地將軍，隆慮侯周灶為隴西將軍，屯三郡。

translations.literal: and invested Marquis of Chang Lu Qing as General of Shang Commandery, Marquis of Ning Wei□ as General of Beidi, and Marquis of Longlü Zhou Zao as General of Longxi, encamped in the three commanderies.
translations.idiomatic: and invested Marquis of Chang Lu Qing as General of Shang Commandery, Marquis of Ning Wei□ as General of Beidi, and Marquis of Longlü Zhou Zao as General of Longxi, encamped in the three commanderies.

sentences.zh: 上親勞軍，勒兵，申教令，賜吏卒，自欲征匈奴。

translations.literal: The Emperor personally comforted the army, arrayed troops, reiterated instructions and orders, bestowed gifts on officers and soldiers, and himself wished to campaign against the Xiongnu.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor personally comforted the army, arrayed the troops, reiterated orders, bestowed gifts on officers and soldiers, and himself wished to campaign against the Xiongnu.

sentences.zh: 群臣諫，不聽；

translations.literal: The ministers remonstrated; he did not heed;
translations.idiomatic: The ministers remonstrated; he did not heed;

sentences.zh: 皇太后固要，上乃止。

translations.literal: the Empress Dowager firmly pressed him, and the Emperor then stopped.
translations.idiomatic: the Empress Dowager firmly pressed him, and the Emperor then stopped.

sentences.zh: 於是以東陽侯張相如為大將軍，成侯董赤、內史欒布皆為將軍，擊匈奴。

translations.literal: Thereupon Marquis of Dongyang Zhang Xiangru was made Grand General, Marquis of Cheng Dong Chi and the Interior Minister Luan Bu were all made generals, and they struck the Xiongnu.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon Marquis of Dongyang Zhang Xiangru was made Grand General, Marquis of Cheng Dong Chi and the Interior Minister Luan Bu were all made generals, and they attacked the Xiongnu.

sentences.zh: 單于留塞內月餘，乃去。

translations.literal: The Chanyu remained within the passes more than a month, then departed.
translations.idiomatic: The Chanyu remained within the passes for more than a month, then departed.

sentences.zh: 漢逐出塞即還，不能有所殺。

translations.literal: Han pursued them out of the passes and then returned, unable to kill anyone.
translations.idiomatic: Han pursued them out of the passes and then returned, unable to kill anyone.
