translations.literal: ----2 The Emperor's carriage passed the Gentlemen's quarters and asked the Gentlemen's Chief Feng Tang: "Where is your father's household?
translations.idiomatic: ----2 The Emperor's carriage passed the Gentlemen's quarters and asked the Gentlemen's Chief Feng Tang: "Where is your father's household?

sentences.zh: 」對曰：「臣大父趙人，父徙代。

translations.literal: " He replied: "Your servant's great-grandfather was a man of Zhao; his father was moved to Dai.
translations.idiomatic: " He replied: "Your servant's great-grandfather was a man of Zhao; his father was moved to Dai.

sentences.zh: 」上曰：「吾居代時，吾尚食監高祛數為我言趙將李齊之賢，戰於巨鹿下。

translations.literal: " The Emperor said: "When I dwelt in Dai, my Master of Victuals Gao Qu several times spoke to me of the worth of Zhao's general Li Qi, fighting below Julu.
translations.idiomatic: " The Emperor said: "When I dwelt in Dai, my Master of Victuals Gao Qu several times told me of the worth of Zhao's general Li Qi, fighting below Julu.

sentences.zh: 今吾每飯意未嘗不在巨鹿也。

translations.literal: Now at every meal my thoughts have never not been at Julu.
translations.idiomatic: Now at every meal my thoughts have never left Julu.

sentences.zh: 父知之乎？

translations.literal: Did your father know of him?
translations.idiomatic: Did your father know of him?

sentences.zh: 」唐對曰：「尚不如廉頗、李牧之為將也。

translations.literal: " Tang replied: "He was still not equal to Lian Po and Li Mu as generals.
translations.idiomatic: " Tang replied: "He was still not equal to Lian Po and Li Mu as generals.

sentences.zh: 」上搏髀曰：「嗟乎！

translations.literal: " The Emperor struck his thigh and said: "Alas!
translations.idiomatic: " The Emperor struck his thigh and said: "Alas!

sentences.zh: 吾獨不得廉頗、李牧為將！

translations.literal: I alone cannot obtain Lian Po and Li Mu as generals!
translations.idiomatic: I alone cannot obtain Lian Po and Li Mu as generals!

sentences.zh: 吾豈憂匈奴哉！

translations.literal: How would I worry about the Xiongnu!
translations.idiomatic: How would I worry about the Xiongnu!

sentences.zh: 」唐曰：「陛下雖得廉頗、李牧，弗能用也。

translations.literal: " Tang said: "Though Your Majesty might obtain Lian Po and Li Mu, you could not employ them.
translations.idiomatic: " Tang said: "Though Your Majesty might obtain Lian Po and Li Mu, you could not employ them.

sentences.zh: 上怒，起，入禁中，良久，召唐，讓曰：「公奈何眾辱我，獨無間處乎！

translations.literal: The Emperor was angry, rose, and entered the inner palace; after a long while he summoned Tang and reproached him: "Sir, why do you publicly humiliate me—is there no private place!
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor was angry, rose, and entered the inner palace; after a long while he summoned Tang and reproached him: "Sir, why do you publicly humiliate me—is there no private place!

sentences.zh: 」唐謝曰：「鄙人不知忌諱。

translations.literal: " Tang apologized: "This rustic does not know taboos.
translations.idiomatic: " Tang apologized: "This rustic does not know taboos.

sentences.zh: 」上方以胡寇為意，乃卒復問唐曰：「公何以知吾不能用廉頗、李牧也？

translations.literal: " The Emperor, just then concerned with Hu bandits, thereupon finally again asked Tang: "How do you know I could not employ Lian Po and Li Mu?
translations.idiomatic: " The Emperor, just then concerned with the Xiongnu, thereupon finally again asked Tang: "How do you know I could not employ Lian Po and Li Mu?

sentences.zh: 」唐對曰：「臣聞上古王者之遣將也，跪而推轂，曰：『閫以內者，寡人制之；

translations.literal: " Tang replied: "Your servant has heard that when ancient kings above dispatched generals, they knelt and pushed the chariot wheel, saying: 'Within the bar I control;
translations.idiomatic: " Tang replied: "Your servant has heard that when ancient kings dispatched generals, they knelt and pushed the chariot wheel, saying: 'Within the bar I control;

sentences.zh: 閫以外者，將軍制之。

translations.literal: without the bar the general controls.
translations.idiomatic: without the bar the general controls.

sentences.zh: 』軍功爵賞皆決於外，歸而奏之，此非虛言也。

translations.literal: ' Military merit, ranks, and rewards are all decided outside; returning he reports—this is not empty talk.
translations.idiomatic: ' Military merit, ranks, and rewards are all decided in the field; on return he reports—this is not empty talk.

sentences.zh: 臣大父言：李牧為趙將，居邊，軍市之租，皆自用饗士；

translations.literal: Your servant's great-grandfather said: Li Mu as Zhao's general dwelt on the border; the army market's rents he all used himself to feast his officers;
translations.idiomatic: Your servant's great-grandfather said: Li Mu as Zhao's general dwelt on the border; the army market's rents he all used himself to feast his officers;

sentences.zh: 賞賜決於外，不從中覆也。

translations.literal: rewards and gifts were decided outside and did not await central overturn.
translations.idiomatic: rewards and gifts were decided in the field and did not await central review.

sentences.zh: 委任而責成功，故李牧乃得盡其智能；

translations.literal: Entrusting him and charging success, therefore Li Mu was able to exhaust his wisdom and ability;
translations.idiomatic: Entrusting him and charging him with success, therefore Li Mu was able to exhaust his wisdom and ability;

sentences.zh: 選車千三百乘，彀騎萬三千，百金之士十萬，是以北逐單于，破東胡，滅澹林，西抑強秦，南支韓、魏。

translations.literal: he selected thirteen hundred chariots, ten thousand three hundred armored horsemen, and one hundred thousand men worth a hundred in gold—thereby north he drove off the Chanyu, broke the Eastern Hu, extinguished the Fulin, west he checked mighty Qin, south he supported Han and Wei.
translations.idiomatic: he selected thirteen hundred chariots, ten thousand three hundred armored horsemen, and one hundred thousand elite warriors—thereby north he drove off the Chanyu, broke the Eastern Hu, extinguished the Fulin, west he checked mighty Qin, south he supported Han and Wei.

sentences.zh: 當是之時，趙幾霸。

translations.literal: At that time Zhao nearly dominated.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Zhao nearly dominated.

sentences.zh: 其後會趙王遷立，用郭開讒，卒誅李牧，令顏聚代之；

translations.literal: Afterward it happened that King Qian of Zhao was established; employing Guo Kai's slander, he finally executed Li Mu and ordered Yan Ju to replace him;
translations.idiomatic: Afterward it happened that King Qian of Zhao was established; employing Guo Kai's slander, he finally executed Li Mu and ordered Yan Ju to replace him;

sentences.zh: 是以兵破士北，為秦所禽滅。

translations.literal: therefore the army was broken, officers fled north, and they were captured and extinguished by Qin.
translations.idiomatic: therefore the army was broken, the troops fled north, and they were captured and destroyed by Qin.

sentences.zh: 今臣竊聞魏尚為雲中守，其軍市租盡以饗士卒，私養錢五日一椎牛，自饗賓客、軍吏、舍人，是以匈奴遠避，不近雲中之塞。

translations.literal: Now your servant has privately heard that Wei Shang is Administrator of Yunzhong; the army market rents he entirely uses to feast soldiers, and from private nurture funds every five days he pounds an ox to feast himself with guests, army officers, and household retainers—therefore the Xiongnu keep far off and do not approach Yunzhong's passes.
translations.idiomatic: Now your servant has privately heard that Wei Shang is Administrator of Yunzhong; the army market rents he entirely uses to feast the soldiers, and from private nurture funds every five days he butchers an ox to feast guests, army officers, and household retainers—therefore the Xiongnu keep far off and do not approach Yunzhong's passes.

sentences.zh: 虜曾一入，尚率車騎擊之，所殺甚眾。

translations.literal: The barbarians once entered; Shang led chariots and horsemen to strike them and killed very many.
translations.idiomatic: The barbarians once invaded; Shang led chariots and horsemen to attack them and killed very many.

sentences.zh: 夫士卒盡家人子，起田中從軍，安知尺籍、伍符！

translations.literal: The soldiers are all sons of families, rising from the fields to join the army—how would they know foot-measure registers and five-man tallies!
translations.idiomatic: The soldiers are all sons of families, rising from the fields to join the army—how would they know roster records and unit tallies!

sentences.zh: 終日力戰，斬首捕虜，上功幕府，一言不相應，文吏以法繩之，其賞不行，而吏奉法必用。

translations.literal: All day they fought with strength, beheaded and captured enemies, and reported merit to the headquarters—if one word did not correspond, the clerkly officers bound them by law; their rewards were not carried out, yet the officers' observance of law was surely applied.
translations.idiomatic: All day they fought hard, beheaded and captured enemies, and reported merit to headquarters—if one word did not match, the clerkly officers bound them by law; their rewards were not granted, yet the officers' enforcement of law was always applied.

sentences.zh: 臣愚以為陛下賞太輕，罰太重。

translations.literal: Your servant foolishly considers that Your Majesty's rewards are too light and punishments too heavy.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant foolishly considers that Your Majesty's rewards are too light and punishments too heavy.

sentences.zh: 且雲中守魏尚坐上功首虜差六級，陛下下之吏，削其爵，罰作之。

translations.literal: Moreover Yunzhong Administrator Wei Shang for his reported merit in enemy heads was short six grades; Your Majesty sent him down to the officers, reduced his rank, and punished him with corvée labor.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover Yunzhong Administrator Wei Shang for his reported merit in enemy heads was short six grades; Your Majesty sent him to the officers, reduced his rank, and punished him with corvée labor.

sentences.zh: 由此言之，陛下雖得廉頗、李牧，弗能用也！

translations.literal: From this speaking, though Your Majesty might obtain Lian Po and Li Mu, you could not employ them!
translations.idiomatic: From this it follows that though Your Majesty might obtain Lian Po and Li Mu, you could not employ them!

sentences.zh: 」上說。

translations.literal: " The Emperor was pleased.
translations.idiomatic: " The Emperor was pleased.

sentences.zh: 是日，令唐持節赦魏尚，復以為雲中守，而拜唐為車騎都尉。

translations.literal: That day he ordered Tang to hold the staff and amnesty Wei Shang, restore him as Administrator of Yunzhong, and invested Tang as Commandant of Chariots and Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: That day he ordered Tang to hold the staff and pardon Wei Shang, restore him as Administrator of Yunzhong, and invested Tang as Commandant of Chariots and Cavalry.

sentences.zh: ----3春，詔廣增諸祀壇場、珪幣，且曰：「吾聞祠官祝釐，皆歸福於朕躬，不為百姓，朕甚愧之。

translations.literal: ----3 In spring an edict broadly increased the sacrificial mounds and fields, jade and silks, and said: "I have heard that the sacrificial officers' prayers for blessing all return good fortune to my person and not to the hundred surnames—I am deeply ashamed.
translations.idiomatic: ----3 In spring an edict broadly increased the sacrificial altars and fields, jade and silks, and said: "I have heard that the sacrificial officers' prayers for blessing all return good fortune to my person and not to the common people—I am deeply ashamed.

sentences.zh: 夫以朕之不德，而專饗獨美其福，百姓不與焉，是重吾不德也。

translations.literal: That with my lack of virtue I alone enjoy and alone beautify the blessing, the hundred surnames not sharing in it—this doubles my lack of virtue.
translations.idiomatic: That with my lack of virtue I alone enjoy and alone claim the blessing, the common people not sharing in it—this doubles my lack of virtue.

sentences.zh: 其令祠官致敬，無有所祈！

translations.literal: Order the sacrificial officers to show reverence and not pray for anything!
translations.idiomatic: Order the sacrificial officers to show reverence and not pray for anything!

sentences.zh: 」----4是歲，河間文王辟強薨。

translations.literal: " ----4 That year King Wen of Hejian Biruqi died.
translations.idiomatic: " ----4 That year King Wen of Hejian Biruqi died.

sentences.zh: ----5初，丞相張蒼以為漢得水德，魯人公孫臣以為漢當土德，其應，黃龍見；

translations.literal: ----5 At first Chancellor Zhang Cang considered that Han obtained the Water Virtue; the Lu man Gongsun Chen considered that Han ought to have the Earth Virtue—its omen: a yellow dragon appeared;
translations.idiomatic: ----5 At first Chancellor Zhang Cang held that Han possessed the Water Virtue; the Lu man Gongsun Chen held that Han ought to possess the Earth Virtue—its omen: a yellow dragon appeared;

sentences.zh: 蒼以為非是，罷之。

translations.literal: Zhang Cang considered it not so and dismissed him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Cang held it incorrect and dismissed him.

sentences.zh: ----1春，黃龍見成紀。

translations.literal: ----1 In spring a yellow dragon appeared at Chengji.
translations.idiomatic: ----1 In spring a yellow dragon appeared at Chengji.

sentences.zh: 帝召公孫臣，拜為博士，與諸生申明土德，草改歷、服色事。

translations.literal: The Emperor summoned Gongsun Chen, invested him as Erudite, and with the various students clarified the Earth Virtue and drafted matters of changing the calendar and garment colors.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor summoned Gongsun Chen, invested him as Erudite, and with the various students clarified the Earth Virtue and drafted matters of changing the calendar and garment colors.

sentences.zh: 張蒼由此自絀。

translations.literal: Zhang Cang thereby humbled himself.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Cang thereby humbled himself.

sentences.zh: ----2夏，四月，上始幸雍，郊見五帝，赦天下。

translations.literal: ----2 In summer, the fourth month, the Emperor first visited Yong, suburban-sacrificed to the Five Emperors, and amnestied all under Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: ----2 In summer, the fourth month, the Emperor first visited Yong, suburban-sacrificed to the Five Emperors, and amnestied the realm.

sentences.zh: ----3九月，詔諸侯王、公卿、郡守舉賢良、能直言極諫者，上親策之。

translations.literal: ----3 In the ninth month an edict ordered feudal kings, high ministers, and commandery administrators to recommend the worthy and good and those able to speak bluntly with extreme remonstrance; the Emperor personally examined them.
translations.idiomatic: ----3 In the ninth month an edict ordered feudal kings, high ministers, and commandery administrators to recommend the worthy and good and those able to speak bluntly with extreme remonstrance; the Emperor personally examined them.

sentences.zh: 太子家令晁錯對策高第，擢為中大夫。

translations.idiomatic: Household Commandant of the Heir Apparent Chao Cuo's examination answer ranked highest; he was promoted to Grand Master of the Palace.

sentences.zh: 錯又上言宜削諸侯及法令可更定者書凡三十篇。

translations.idiomatic: Cuo also submitted that feudal lords ought to be reduced and statutes that could be revised, thirty memorials in all.

sentences.zh: 上雖不盡聽，然奇其材。

translations.literal: The Emperor though he did not fully heed him yet marveled at his talent.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor though he did not fully heed him yet marveled at his talent.

sentences.zh: ----4是歲，齊文王則、河間哀王福皆薨，無子，國除。

translations.literal: ----4 That year King Wen of Qi Ze and King Ai of Hejian Fu all died without sons; their states were abolished.
translations.idiomatic: ----4 That year King Wen of Qi Ze and King Ai of Hejian Fu all died without sons; their states were abolished.

sentences.zh: ----5趙人新垣平以望氣見上，言長安東北有神氣，成五采，於是作渭陽五帝廟。

translations.literal: ----5 The Zhao man Xinyuan Ping, by observing qi, had audience with the Emperor and said that northeast of Chang'an there was divine qi forming five colors; thereupon the Weiyang Five Emperors Temple was built.
translations.idiomatic: ----5 The Zhao man Xinyuan Ping, by observing qi, had audience with the Emperor and said that northeast of Chang'an there was divine qi forming five colors; thereupon the Weiyang Five Emperors Temple was built.

sentences.zh: ----1夏，四月，上郊祀上帝於渭陽五帝廟。

translations.literal: ----1 In summer, the fourth month, the Emperor suburban-sacrificed to the High God at the Weiyang Five Emperors Temple.
translations.idiomatic: ----1 In summer, the fourth month, the Emperor suburban-sacrificed to the High God at the Weiyang Five Emperors Temple.

sentences.zh: 於是貴新垣平至上大夫，賜累千金；

translations.literal: Thereupon Xinyuan Ping was honored to Grand Master of the Palace and given gifts accumulating to a thousand in gold;
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon Xinyuan Ping was honored to Grand Master of the Palace and given gifts accumulating to a thousand in gold;

sentences.zh: 而使博士、諸生刺《六經》中作《王制》，謀議巡狩、封禪事。

translations.literal: and he had Erudites and various students pick through the Six Classics to compose the Royal Regulations and deliberate on imperial tours and feng and shan affairs.
translations.idiomatic: and he had Erudites and various students pick through the Six Classics to compose the Royal Regulations and deliberate on imperial tours and feng and shan affairs.

sentences.zh: 又於長門道北立五帝壇。

translations.literal: He also established a Five Emperors mound north of Changmen Road.
translations.idiomatic: He also established a Five Emperors altar north of Changmen Road.

sentences.zh: ----2徙淮南王喜復為城陽王，又分齊為六國；

translations.literal: ----2 King Xi of Huainan was moved and restored as King of Chengyang; Qi was again divided into six states;
translations.idiomatic: ----2 King Xi of Huainan was moved and restored as King of Chengyang; Qi was again divided into six states;

sentences.zh: 丙寅，立齊悼惠王子在者六人：楊虛侯將閭為齊王，安都侯志為濟北王，武成侯賢為菑川王，白石侯雄渠為膠東王，平昌侯卬為膠西王，扐侯辟光為濟南王。

translations.literal: On bingyin the six surviving sons of King Daohui of Qi were established: Marquis of Yangxu Jiang Lü as King of Qi, Marquis of Andu Zhi as King of Jibei, Marquis of Wucheng Xian as King of Zichuan, Marquis of Baishi Xiongqu as King of Jiaodong, Marquis of Pingchang Ang as King of Jiaoxi, and Marquis of Yi Piguang as King of Jinan.
translations.idiomatic: On bingyin the six surviving sons of King Daohui of Qi were established: Marquis of Yangxu Jiang Lü as King of Qi, Marquis of Andu Zhi as King of Jibei, Marquis of Wucheng Xian as King of Zichuan, Marquis of Baishi Xiongqu as King of Jiaodong, Marquis of Pingchang Ang as King of Jiaoxi, and Marquis of Yi Piguang as King of Jinan.

sentences.zh: 淮南厲王子在者三人：阜陵安為淮南王，安陽侯勃為衡山王，陽周侯賜為廬江王。

translations.literal: The three surviving sons of King Li of Huainan: Fu'an as King of Huainan, Marquis of Anyang Bo as King of Hengshan, and Marquis of Yangzhou Ci as King of Lujiang.
translations.idiomatic: The three surviving sons of King Li of Huainan: Fu'an as King of Huainan, Marquis of Anyang Bo as King of Hengshan, and Marquis of Yangzhou Ci as King of Lujiang.

sentences.zh: ----3秋，九月，新垣平使人持玉杯上書闕下獻之。

translations.literal: ----3 In autumn, the ninth month, Xinyuan Ping sent a man holding a jade cup to submit a letter below the palace gate and present it.
translations.idiomatic: ----3 In autumn, the ninth month, Xinyuan Ping sent a man holding a jade cup to submit a letter below the palace gate and present it.

sentences.zh: 平言上曰：「闕下有寶玉氣來者。

translations.literal: Ping spoke to the Emperor: "Below the gate there is jade treasure qi coming.
translations.idiomatic: Ping spoke to the Emperor: "Below the gate there is jade treasure qi coming.

sentences.zh: 」已，視之，果有獻玉杯者，刻曰「人主延壽」。

translations.literal: " Shortly after, they looked and indeed there was one presenting a jade cup, inscribed: "The ruler prolongs life."
translations.idiomatic: " Shortly after, they looked and indeed there was one presenting a jade cup, inscribed: "The ruler prolongs life."

sentences.zh: 平又言：「臣侯日再中。

translations.literal: Ping also said: "Your servant awaits the sun reaching zenith twice.
translations.idiomatic: Ping also said: "Your servant awaits the sun reaching zenith twice.

sentences.zh: 」居頃之，日卻，復中。

translations.literal: " After a short while the sun retreated and again reached zenith.
translations.idiomatic: " After a short while the sun retreated and again reached zenith.

sentences.zh: 於是始更以十七年為元年，令天下大酺。

translations.literal: Thereupon he first changed to take the seventeenth year as the inaugural year and ordered a great communal feast for all under Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon he first changed to take the seventeenth year as the inaugural year and ordered a great communal feast for the realm.

sentences.zh: 平言曰：「周鼎亡在泗水中。

translations.literal: Ping said: "The Zhou cauldrons were lost in the Si River.
translations.idiomatic: Ping said: "The Zhou cauldrons were lost in the Si River.

sentences.zh: 今河決，通於泗，臣望東北汾陰直有金寶氣，意周鼎其出乎！

translations.literal: Now the Yellow River has burst and connects to the Si; your servant observed northeast of Fenyin directly that there is gold and treasure qi—I believe the Zhou cauldrons will emerge!
translations.idiomatic: Now the Yellow River has burst and connects to the Si; your servant observed northeast of Fenyin directly that there is gold and treasure qi—I believe the Zhou cauldrons will emerge!

sentences.zh: 兆見，不迎則不至。

translations.literal: The omen has appeared; if not welcomed they will not arrive.
translations.idiomatic: The omen has appeared; if not welcomed they will not arrive.

sentences.zh: 」於是上使使治廟汾陰南，臨河，欲祠出周鼎。

translations.literal: " Thereupon the Emperor sent envoys to build a temple south of Fenyin facing the river, wishing to sacrifice and draw out the Zhou cauldrons.
translations.idiomatic: " Thereupon the Emperor sent envoys to build a temple south of Fenyin facing the river, wishing to sacrifice and draw out the Zhou cauldrons.

sentences.zh: ----1冬，十月，人有上書告新垣平「所言諧詐也」；

translations.literal: ----1 In winter, the tenth month, someone submitted a letter reporting Xinyuan Ping "his words are harmoniously deceitful";
translations.idiomatic: ----1 In winter, the tenth month, someone submitted a letter reporting Xinyuan Ping "his words are harmoniously deceitful";

sentences.zh: 下吏治，誅夷平。

translations.literal: he was sent down to the officers for trial and Ping was executed and his clan exterminated.
translations.idiomatic: he was sent to the officers for trial and Ping was executed and his clan exterminated.

sentences.zh: 是後，上亦怠於改正、服、鬼神之事，而渭陽、長門五帝，使祠官領，以時致禮，不往焉。

translations.literal: After this the Emperor also grew slack toward correcting the calendar, garments, and spirit matters; as for the Weiyang and Changmen Five Emperors, he had sacrificial officers oversee them, presenting rites on schedule, and did not go himself.
translations.idiomatic: After this the Emperor also grew slack toward correcting the calendar, garments, and spirit matters; as for the Weiyang and Changmen Five Emperors, he had sacrificial officers oversee them, presenting rites on schedule, and did not go himself.

sentences.zh: ----2春，三月，孝惠皇后張氏薨。

translations.literal: ----2 In spring, the third month, Empress Zhang of Xiaohui died.
translations.idiomatic: ----2 In spring, the third month, Empress Zhang of Xiaohui died.

sentences.zh: ----3詔曰：「間者數年不登，又有水旱、疾疫之災，朕甚憂之。

translations.literal: ----3 An edict said: "Of late for several years harvests have not succeeded, and again there are flood, drought, and pestilence disasters—I am deeply troubled.
translations.idiomatic: ----3 An edict ran: "Harvests have failed several years running, and flood, drought, and plague have followed. I am deeply troubled.

sentences.zh: 愚而不明，未達其咎：意者朕之政有所失而行有過與？

translations.literal: Stupid and not enlightened, I have not reached its blame: perhaps my government has something lost and my conduct has faults?
translations.idiomatic: I am dull and cannot see the cause: has my rule gone wrong, or my conduct strayed?

sentences.zh: 乃天道有不順，地利或不得，人事多失和，鬼神廢不享與？

translations.literal: Or is it that Heaven's Way is not compliant, Earth's advantage perhaps not obtained, human affairs mostly lose harmony, and ghosts and spirits are neglected and not offered to?
translations.idiomatic: Or has Heaven turned aside, earth withheld its bounty, men fallen out of harmony, or spirits been neglected so they receive no offerings?

sentences.zh: 何以致此？

translations.literal: What brings this about?
translations.idiomatic: What has brought this about?

sentences.zh: 將百官之奉養或廢，無用之事或多與？

translations.literal: Perhaps the hundred officials' sustenance is neglected, or useless affairs are many?
translations.idiomatic: Are officials' stipends wasted, or useless undertakings multiplied?

sentences.zh: 何其民食之寡乏也？

translations.literal: How is it that the people's food is so scant and lacking?
translations.idiomatic: Why is the people's food so scarce?

sentences.zh: 夫度田非益寡，而計民未加益，以口量地，其於古猶有餘，而食之甚不足者，其咎安在？

translations.literal: Now measured fields are not more scant, yet counted people have not increased—measuring land by mouths, compared with antiquity there is still surplus, yet eating is very insufficient—where does the blame lie?
translations.idiomatic: Measured acreage has not shrunk, and the population has not grown; by heads per field we still match antiquity with land to spare—yet food falls far short. Where does the fault lie?

sentences.zh: 無乃百姓之從事於末以害農者蕃，為酒醪以靡谷者多，六畜之食焉者眾與？

translations.literal: Perhaps it is not that the hundred people engage in the secondary to harm farming in great numbers, make ale and brew to waste grain in many cases, and those who feed on the six livestock are numerous?
translations.idiomatic: Is it that too many folk chase trade and commerce at farming's expense, that brewing wastes grain, or that too many beasts are fed at men's cost?

sentences.zh: 細大之義，吾未得其中，其與丞相、列侯、吏二千石、博士議之。

translations.literal: The fine and great principles—I have not obtained their center; let them discuss it with the Chancellor, ranked marquises, officials of two thousand piculs, and erudites.
translations.idiomatic: I cannot yet strike the balance between large policy and small detail; let the Chancellor, the marquises, the two-thousand-picul officials, and the erudites debate it.

sentences.zh: 有可以佐百姓者，率意遠思，無有所隱！

translations.literal: Whatever can assist the hundred people—follow your intent and think far—hide nothing!
translations.idiomatic: Whatever may aid the people, speak your mind freely and think far ahead—conceal nothing!

sentences.zh: 」----1夏，上行幸雍棫陽宮。

translations.literal: " ----1 In summer, the Emperor traveled in favor to Yong's Zhiyang Palace.
translations.idiomatic: " ----1 That summer the Emperor went to the Zhiyang Palace at Yong.

sentences.zh: ----2六月，代孝王參薨。

translations.literal: ----2 In the sixth month, Dai's Prince Xiao Liu Can died.
translations.idiomatic: ----2 In the sixth month Dai's Prince Xiao, Liu Can, died.

sentences.zh: ----3匈奴連歲入邊，殺略人民、畜產甚多；

translations.literal: ----3 The Xiongnu for successive years entered the border, killing and plundering the people and livestock in great numbers;
translations.idiomatic: ----3 The Xiongnu raided the frontier year after year, killing and carrying off people and herds in great numbers;

sentences.zh: 雲中、遼東最甚，郡萬餘人。

translations.literal: Yunzhong and Liaodong suffered most severely—tens of thousands per commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Yunzhong and Liaodong suffered worst, with more than ten thousand victims in each commandery.

sentences.zh: 上患之，乃使使遺匈奴書。

translations.literal: The Emperor was troubled by it and therefore sent envoys to deliver a letter to the Xiongnu.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor, troubled, sent envoys with a letter to the Xiongnu.

sentences.zh: 單于亦使當戶報謝，復與匈奴和親。

translations.literal: The chanyu also sent the danghu in reply with thanks, and again made peace and kinship with the Xiongnu.
translations.idiomatic: The chanyu sent the danghu in reply with thanks, and the two sides renewed the peace marriage.

sentences.zh: ----4八月，戊戌，丞相張蒼免。

translations.literal: ----4 In the eighth month, on wuxu, Chancellor Zhang Cang was dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: ----4 In the eighth month, on the day wuxu, Chancellor Zhang Cang was removed.

sentences.zh: 帝以皇后弟竇廣國賢，有行，欲相之，曰：「恐天下以吾私廣國，久念不可。

translations.literal: The Emperor because the Empress's younger brother Dou Guangguo was worthy and had conduct wished to make him Chancellor, saying: "I fear all under Heaven will take that I favor Guangguo privately—long I have considered it and cannot.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor thought the Empress's brother Dou Guangguo worthy and upright and wished to make him Chancellor, but said, "I fear the realm will think I favor Guangguo for private reasons; I have long weighed it and cannot do it.

sentences.zh: 」而高帝時大臣，餘見無可者。

translations.literal: " Yet among the great ministers of High Emperor's time, of those remaining seen, there was none acceptable.
translations.idiomatic: " Among the great ministers who had served Gaozu, none who remained seemed fit.

sentences.zh: 御史大夫梁國申屠嘉，故以材官蹶張從高帝，封關內侯；

translations.literal: Grandee Secretary Liang's Shen Tujia—formerly as a skilled soldier with crossbow-draw followed High Emperor, was enfeoffed Marquis within the Passes;
translations.idiomatic: Grandee Secretary Shen Tujia of Liang—once a crossbow-skilled warrior who followed Gaozu—had been enfeoffed as a marquis within the passes;

sentences.zh: 庚午，以嘉為丞相，封故安侯。

translations.literal: on gengwu, Jia was made Chancellor and enfeoffed as Marquis of Gu'an.
translations.idiomatic: on the day gengwu he was made Chancellor and enfeoffed as Marquis of Gu'an.

sentences.zh: 嘉為人廉直，門不受私謁。

translations.literal: Jia as a man was incorrupt and upright; his gate did not receive private calls.
translations.idiomatic: Jia was upright and incorrupt; his gate accepted no private callers.

sentences.zh: 是時，太中大夫鄧通方愛幸，賞賜累巨萬。

translations.literal: At this time Grand Master of the Palace Deng Tong was just favored and cherished; rewards and grants piled to tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Grand Master Deng Tong was in special favor, and rewards to him piled into the tens of thousands.

sentences.zh: 帝嘗燕飲通家，其寵幸無比。

translations.literal: The Emperor once feasted and drank at Tong's house; his favor and cherishing had no peer.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor once feasted at Tong's house; no favorite ever matched him.

sentences.zh: 嘉嘗入朝，而通居上旁，有怠慢之禮，嘉奏事畢，因言曰：「陛下幸愛群臣，則富貴之；

translations.literal: Jia once entered court, and Tong sat beside the Emperor with a negligent manner of ritual; when Jia had finished reporting affairs, he therefore said: "Your Majesty, if you favor and love the host of ministers, then enrich and ennoble them;
translations.idiomatic: Once when Jia attended court, Tong sat beside the Emperor with negligent manners. When Jia had finished his business he said, "Your Majesty, if you cherish your ministers, make them rich and noble;

sentences.zh: 至於朝廷之禮，不可以不肅。

translations.literal: as for court ritual, it cannot be not solemn.
translations.idiomatic: but court ritual must not be treated lightly.

sentences.zh: 」上曰：「君勿言，吾私之。

translations.literal: " The Emperor said: "Lord, do not speak—I favor him privately.
translations.idiomatic: " The Emperor said, "Say no more; he is my private favorite.

sentences.zh: 」罷朝，坐府中，嘉為檄召通詣丞相府，不來，且斬通。

translations.literal: " Court dismissed, sitting in his headquarters, Jia made a dispatch summoning Tong to come to the Chancellor's headquarters; if he did not come, he would behead Tong.
translations.idiomatic: " After court Jia sat in his office and sent a summons ordering Tong to the Chancellor's house on pain of execution if he failed to come.

sentences.zh: 通恐，入言上；

translations.literal: Tong was afraid and entered to tell the Emperor;
translations.idiomatic: Tong, afraid, went in and told the Emperor;

sentences.zh: 上曰：「汝第往，吾今使人召若。

translations.literal: the Emperor said: "You just go—I will now send men to summon you.
translations.idiomatic: the Emperor said, "Go for now; I will send men to fetch you.

sentences.zh: 」通詣丞相，免冠、徒跣，頓首謝嘉。

translations.literal: " Tong went to the Chancellor, removed cap, went barefoot, and knocked head to thank Jia.
translations.idiomatic: " Tong went to the Chancellor, bareheaded and barefoot, and kowtowed to beg Jia's pardon.

sentences.zh: 嘉坐自如，弗為禮，責曰：「夫朝廷者，高帝之朝廷也。

translations.literal: Jia sat as before, did not perform ritual, and reproached him: "Now the court is High Emperor's court.
translations.idiomatic: Jia sat as before, made no courtesy, and rebuked him: "The court is Gaozu's court.

sentences.zh: 通小臣，戲殿上，大不敬，當斬。

translations.literal: Tong is a petty minister who sported on the hall—great irreverence; he should be beheaded.
translations.idiomatic: You are a petty minister who played the fool in the hall—grave irreverence, punishable by death.

sentences.zh: 吏！

translations.literal: Clerks!
translations.idiomatic: Officers!

sentences.zh: 今行斬之！

translations.literal: Now carry out beheading him!
translations.idiomatic: Behead him at once!

sentences.zh: 」通頓首，首盡出血，不解。

translations.literal: " Tong knocked his head until the head was all bleeding, yet was not released.
translations.idiomatic: " Tong kowtowed until his head bled, yet was not released.

sentences.zh: 上度丞相已困通，使使持節召通而謝丞相：「此吾弄臣，君釋之！

translations.literal: The Emperor estimated the Chancellor had already cornered Tong, sent an envoy bearing credentials to summon Tong and apologize to the Chancellor: "This is my plaything minister—lord, release him!
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor judged the Chancellor had cornered Tong, sent an envoy with credentials to summon Tong, and told the Chancellor, "He is my plaything—release him!

sentences.zh: 」鄧通既至，為上泣曰：「丞相幾殺臣！

translations.literal: " When Deng Tong had arrived, he wept to the Emperor: "The Chancellor nearly killed your servant!
translations.idiomatic: " When Deng Tong arrived he wept to the Emperor, "The Chancellor nearly killed me!

sentences.zh: 」----1春，二月，上行幸代。

translations.literal: " ----1 In spring, the second month, the Emperor traveled in favor to Dai.
translations.idiomatic: " ----1 In spring, the second month, the Emperor went to Dai.

sentences.zh: ----2是歲，匈奴老上單于死，子軍臣單于立。

translations.literal: ----2 This year the Xiongnu Laoshang Chanyu died; his son Junchen Chanyu was installed.
translations.idiomatic: ----2 That year the Xiongnu chanyu Laoshang died and his son Junchen succeeded as chanyu.

sentences.zh: ----1夏，四月，丙寅晦，日有食之。

translations.literal: ----1 In summer, the fourth month, on the last day of the sexagenary cycle bingyin, there was an eclipse of the sun.
translations.idiomatic: ----1 In summer, the fourth month, on the last day bingyin, the sun was eclipsed.

sentences.zh: ----2五月，赦天下。

translations.literal: ----2 In the fifth month, he pardoned all under Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: ----2 In the fifth month he proclaimed a general amnesty.

sentences.zh: ----3上行幸雍。

translations.literal: ----3 The Emperor traveled in favor to Yong.
translations.idiomatic: ----3 The Emperor went to Yong.

sentences.zh: ----1春，正月，上行幸隴西；

translations.literal: ----1 In spring, the first month, the Emperor traveled in favor to Longxi;
translations.idiomatic: ----1 In spring, the first month, the Emperor went to Longxi;

sentences.zh: 三月，行幸雍；

translations.literal: in the third month, he traveled in favor to Yong;
translations.idiomatic: in the third month he went to Yong;

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，行幸代。

translations.literal: in autumn, the seventh month, he traveled in favor to Dai.
translations.idiomatic: in autumn, the seventh month, he went to Dai.

sentences.zh: ----1冬，匈奴三萬騎入上郡，三萬騎入雲中，所殺略甚眾，烽火通於甘泉、長安。

translations.literal: ----1 In winter, the Xiongnu with thirty thousand horsemen entered Shang commandery and thirty thousand horsemen entered Yunzhong; what they killed and plundered was very numerous—beacon fires connected to Ganquan and Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: ----1 In winter thirty thousand Xiongnu horsemen entered Shang commandery and thirty thousand entered Yunzhong; the killing and plunder were heavy, and beacon fires lit the sky from Ganquan to Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 以中大夫令免為車騎將軍，屯飛狐；

translations.literal: Central Grandee Ling Mian was made General of Chariots and Cavalry and encamped at Flying Fox;
translations.idiomatic: Central Grandee Ling Mian was made General of Chariots and Cavalry and encamped at Flying Fox;

sentences.zh: 故楚相蘇意為將軍，屯句注；

translations.literal: former Chancellor of Chu Su Yi was made General and encamped at Gouzhu;
translations.idiomatic: former Chancellor of Chu Su Yi was made general and encamped at Gouzhu;

sentences.zh: 將軍張武屯北地；

translations.literal: General Zhang Wu encamped at Beidi;
translations.idiomatic: General Zhang Wu encamped in Beidi;

sentences.zh: 河內太守周亞夫為將軍，次細柳；

translations.literal: Administrator of Henei Zhou Yafu was made General and stationed at Fine Willow;
translations.idiomatic: Administrator of Henei Zhou Yafu was made general and posted at Fine Willow;

sentences.zh: 宗正劉禮為將軍，次霸上，祝茲侯徐厲為將軍，次棘門；

translations.literal: Director of the Imperial Clan Liu Li was made General and stationed at Bashang; Marquis of Zhuzi Xu Li was made General and stationed at Jimen;
translations.idiomatic: Director of the Imperial Clan Liu Li was made general and posted at Bashang; Marquis of Zhuzi Xu Li was made general and posted at Jimen;

sentences.zh: 以備胡。

translations.literal: to prepare against the Hu.
translations.idiomatic: to guard against the barbarians.

sentences.zh: 上自勞軍，至霸上及棘門軍，直馳入，將以下騎送迎。

translations.literal: The Emperor himself went to comfort the armies; arriving at the Bashang and Jimen armies, he drove straight in—the generals and below dismounted on horseback to escort and welcome.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor went in person to review the troops. At Bashang and Jimen he drove straight in, and the generals and their men dismounted to escort and welcome him.

sentences.zh: 已而之細柳軍，軍士吏被甲，銳兵刃，彀弓弩持滿，天子先驅至，不得入。

translations.literal: Afterward he went to the Fine Willow army; soldiers and officers wore armor, weapons were sharp, bows and crossbows were drawn full—when the Son of Heaven's vanguard arrived, it could not enter.
translations.idiomatic: Then he came to Fine Willow. Soldiers and officers wore armor; blades were sharp; bows and crossbows were strung and drawn. When the Emperor's vanguard arrived, it was not admitted.

sentences.zh: 先驅曰：「天子且至！

translations.literal: The vanguard said: "The Son of Heaven is about to arrive!
translations.idiomatic: The vanguard called, "The Son of Heaven is coming!

sentences.zh: 」軍門都尉曰；

translations.literal: " The army-gate commandant said;
translations.idiomatic: " The commandant of the camp gate replied;

sentences.zh: 「將軍令曰：『軍中聞將軍令，不聞天子之詔！

translations.literal: "The General's order says: "In the army one hears the General's orders, not the Son of Heaven's edicts!
translations.idiomatic: "The general's order runs: In camp we heed the general's command, not the Son of Heaven's edict!

sentences.zh: 』」居無何，上至，又不得入。

translations.literal: "'" After not long, when the Emperor arrived above, again he could not enter.
translations.idiomatic: "'" Before long the Emperor himself arrived and again was refused entry.

sentences.zh: 於是上乃使使持節詔將軍：「吾欲入營勞軍。

translations.literal: Thereupon the Emperor then sent an envoy bearing credentials to announce to the General: "I wish to enter the camp and comfort the army.
translations.idiomatic: Then the Emperor sent an envoy with credentials to announce to the general, "I wish to enter the camp and review the troops.

sentences.zh: 」亞夫乃傳言「開壁門」。

translations.literal: " Yafu then transmitted the word "Open the rampart gate."
translations.idiomatic: " Yafu passed the order, "Open the gate."

sentences.zh: 壁門士請車騎曰：「將軍約：軍中不得驅馳。

translations.literal: The rampart-gate soldiers requested of the chariots and horsemen: "The General's stipulation: in the army one must not drive at a gallop.
translations.idiomatic: Men at the gate told the riders, "The general's rule: no galloping in camp.

sentences.zh: 」於是天子乃按轡徐行。

translations.literal: " Thereupon the Son of Heaven then held the reins and went slowly.
translations.idiomatic: " Thereupon the Emperor reined in and advanced at a walk.

sentences.zh: 至營，將軍亞夫持兵揖曰：「介冑之士不拜，請以軍禮見。

translations.literal: Arriving at the camp, General Yafu held weapons and bowed with clasped hands: "A man in armor and helmet does not prostrate—please let me be seen with army ritual.
translations.idiomatic: At the camp General Yafu, armed, saluted with clasped hands and said, "An armored man does not kowtow; allow me to greet you by military rites.

sentences.zh: 」天子為動，改容，式車，使人稱謝：「皇帝敬勞將軍。

translations.literal: " The Son of Heaven was moved, changed countenance, leaned on the carriage crossbar, and had a man speak thanks: "The Emperor respectfully comforts the General.
translations.idiomatic: " The Emperor was stirred, changed expression, leaned from the carriage rail, and sent word of thanks: "The Emperor respectfully salutes the general.

sentences.zh: 」成禮而去。

translations.literal: " The rites completed, he departed.
translations.idiomatic: " When the rites were finished he departed.

sentences.zh: 既出軍門，群臣皆驚。

translations.literal: Once he had left the army gate, the host of ministers were all startled.
translations.idiomatic: After he left the camp gate the ministers were all astonished.

sentences.zh: 上曰：「嗟乎，此真將軍矣！

translations.literal: The Emperor said: "Alas, this is a true general!
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor said, "Ah—there is a true general!

sentences.zh: 曩者霸上、棘門軍若兒戲耳，其將固可襲而虜也。

translations.literal: Formerly the Bashang and Jimen armies were like child's play—their generals could indeed be raided and captured.
translations.idiomatic: Bashang and Jimen were child's play; their generals could have been surprised and taken.

sentences.zh: 至於亞夫，可得而犯耶！

translations.literal: As for Yafu, could one obtain and violate him!
translations.idiomatic: As for Yafu—who could touch him!

sentences.zh: 」稱善者久之。

translations.literal: " He praised the goodness for a long while.
translations.idiomatic: " He praised him at length.

sentences.zh: 月餘，漢後至邊，匈奴亦遠塞，漢兵亦罷。

translations.literal: After more than a month, Han arrived late at the border; the Xiongnu also went far from the frontier passes, and Han troops also stood down.
translations.idiomatic: More than a month later Han forces reached the border; the Xiongnu had already withdrawn deep beyond the passes, and the Han armies were stood down.

sentences.zh: 乃拜周亞夫為中尉。

translations.literal: Thereupon Zhou Yafu was appointed Commandant of the Capital.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Yafu was then appointed Commandant of the Capital.

sentences.zh: ----2夏，四月，大旱，蝗。

translations.literal: ----2 In summer, the fourth month, great drought and locusts.
translations.idiomatic: ----2 In summer, the fourth month, severe drought and locusts.

sentences.zh: 令諸侯無入貢；

translations.literal: He ordered the feudal lords not to enter tribute;
translations.idiomatic: He ordered the feudal lords to send no tribute;

sentences.zh: 弛山澤，減諸服御，損郎吏員；

translations.literal: relaxed mountain and marsh levies, reduced various garments and equipage, cut the number of gentleman-attendants;
translations.idiomatic: lifted levies on hills and marshes, cut court wardrobe and equipage, and reduced attendant officers;

sentences.zh: 發倉庾以振民；

translations.literal: opened granaries to relieve the people;
translations.idiomatic: opened the granaries to relieve the people;

sentences.zh: 民得賣爵。

translations.literal: the people were allowed to sell noble ranks.
translations.idiomatic: commoners were permitted to buy noble rank for grain.

sentences.zh: ----1夏，六月，已亥，帝崩於未央宮。

translations.literal: ----1 In summer, the sixth month, on jihai, the Emperor collapsed at Weiyang Palace.
translations.idiomatic: ----1 In summer, the sixth month, on the day jihai, the Emperor died in Weiyang Palace.

sentences.zh: 遺詔曰：:「朕聞之：蓋天下萬物之萌生，靡有不死。

translations.literal: The testamentary edict said: :« I have heard: broadly, of all things born and sprouting under Heaven, none lack death.
translations.idiomatic: His testament ran: :« I have heard that everything born under Heaven must die.

sentences.zh: 死者，天地之理，物之自然，奚可甚哀！

translations.literal: The dead are Heaven and Earth's pattern and things' nature—how can one greatly mourn!
translations.idiomatic: Death is Heaven and earth's law and every creature's nature—why mourn excessively?

sentences.zh: 當今之世，咸嘉生而惡死，厚葬以破業，重服以傷生，吾甚不取。

translations.literal: In the present age, all rejoice in life and hate death; thick burial breaks one's estate, heavy mourning harms the living—I very much do not take it.
translations.idiomatic: Men today rejoice in life and hate death, ruin their estates with lavish funerals, and harm the living with prolonged mourning—I want none of it.

sentences.zh: 且朕既不德，無在佐百姓；

translations.literal: Moreover I am already without virtue and have not been present to assist the hundred people;
translations.idiomatic: Moreover I have lacked virtue and done little to aid the people;

sentences.zh: 今崩，又使重服久臨以罹寒暑之數，哀人父子，傷長老之志，損其飲食，絕鬼神之祭祀，以重吾不德，謂天下何！

translations.literal: now upon collapse, again to make heavy mourning and long attendance so as to suffer cold and heat's reckonings, grieve men father and son, wound elders' wills, harm their food and drink, cut off ghosts and spirits' sacrifices—to double my lack of virtue—what would one say to all under Heaven!
translations.idiomatic: now at my death to impose heavy mourning and long vigils, exposing mourners to heat and cold, grieving fathers and sons, wounding elders, spoiling their food and drink, and cutting off sacrifices to the spirits—would that not double my want of virtue? What could I say to the realm!

sentences.zh: 朕獲保宗廟，以眇眇之身托於天下君王之上，二十有餘年矣。

translations.literal: I have obtained to preserve the ancestral temple, and with this tiny body been entrusted above the realm's lords and kings for twenty-odd years.
translations.idiomatic: I have preserved the ancestral temple and, tiny as I am, held the throne above the realm's kings for more than twenty years.

sentences.zh: 賴天之靈，社稷之福，方內安寧，靡有兵革。

translations.literal: Relying on Heaven's numinous power and the altars of soil and grain's blessing, within the four quarters there is peace and quiet, without arms and armor.
translations.idiomatic: By Heaven's grace and the state's good fortune the realm within the four seas has been tranquil, without war.

sentences.zh: 朕既不敏，常畏過行以羞先帝之遺德，惟年之久長，懼於不終。

translations.literal: I am already not keen, constantly fearing faulty conduct to shame the Former Emperor's bequeathed virtue; only that the years have been long, I feared not reaching the end.
translations.idiomatic: I have not been clever and have often feared that faults would shame the virtue Gaozu left; only the length of years made me fear I might not finish my course.

sentences.zh: 今乃幸以天年得復供養於高廟，其奚哀念之有！

translations.literal: Now I have fortunately by Heaven's years obtained again to be offered at the High Temple—what is there to mourn and remember!
translations.idiomatic: Now I have the good fortune to die in my full years and again to be honored in the High Temple—what is there to mourn!

sentences.zh: 其令天下吏民：令到，出臨三日，皆釋服；

translations.literal: Let it order the realm's clerks and people: when the order arrives, go out and attend mourning three days, then all release mourning garments;
translations.idiomatic: Let all officials and people throughout the realm: when this order arrives, mourn three days abroad, then lay mourning aside;

sentences.zh: 毋禁取婦、嫁女、祠祀、飲酒、食肉，自當給喪事服臨者，皆無跣；

translations.literal: do not forbid taking wives, marrying daughters, sacrifices, drinking wine, or eating meat; those who should themselves supply funeral affairs and attend mourning—all without going barefoot;
translations.idiomatic: do not forbid weddings, sacrifices, wine, or meat; those who must attend the funeral need not go barefoot;

sentences.zh: 絰帶毋過三寸；

translations.literal: hemp bands must not exceed three inches;
translations.idiomatic: mourning sashes must not exceed three inches;

sentences.zh: 毋布車及兵器；

translations.literal: no cloth-covered chariots or weapons;
translations.idiomatic: no draped funeral carts or weapons;

sentences.zh: 毋發民哭臨宮殿中；

translations.literal: do not mobilize the people to weep and attend mourning within the palace halls;
translations.idiomatic: do not summon the people to wail within the palace;

sentences.zh: 殿中當臨者，皆以旦夕各十五舉音，禮畢罷；

translations.literal: those in the halls who should attend mourning—all at dawn and dusk each fifteen utterances of sound; when the rite is finished, stop;
translations.idiomatic: those who mourn in the halls shall wail fifteen cries at dawn and dusk, then cease when the rite is done;

sentences.zh: 非旦夕臨時，禁毋得擅哭臨；

translations.literal: outside dawn and dusk attendance times, forbid that anyone may on his own weep and attend mourning;
translations.idiomatic: at other times none may wail on his own;

sentences.zh: 已下棺，服大功十五日，小功十四日，纖七日，釋服。

translations.literal: after the coffin is lowered, wear great mourning fifteen days, lesser mourning fourteen days, finest mourning seven days, then release garments.
translations.idiomatic: after the coffin is lowered, wear great mourning fifteen days, lesser fourteen, finest seven, then lay mourning aside.

sentences.zh: 它不在令中者，皆以此令比類從事。

translations.literal: Other matters not in the order—all take this order as analogy and category in practice.
translations.idiomatic: Whatever this order does not cover, follow it by analogy.

sentences.zh: 佈告天下，使明知朕意。

translations.literal: Proclaim to all under Heaven, causing all clearly to know my intent.
translations.idiomatic: Proclaim this throughout the realm so all may know my intent clearly.

sentences.zh: 霸陵山川因其故，毋有所改。

translations.literal: At Baling's hills and streams follow their former state—change nothing.
translations.idiomatic: At Baling let hills and streams remain as they are; alter nothing.

sentences.zh: 歸夫以下至少使。

translations.literal: Send home wives and below down to the least envoy.
translations.idiomatic: Send home the palace women down to the lowest attendants.

sentences.zh: 乙巳，葬霸陵。

translations.literal: On yisi, buried at Baling tomb.
translations.idiomatic: On the day yisi, he was buried at Baling.

sentences.zh: 帝即位二十三年，宮室、苑囿、車騎、服御，無所增益；

translations.literal: The Emperor in the twenty-three years since taking the throne—palaces, parks, chariots and horses, garments and equipage—nothing was increased;
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-three years of his reign the Emperor added nothing to palaces, parks, chariots, horses, or court wardrobe;

sentences.zh: 有不便，輒馳以利民。

translations.literal: when there was inconvenience, he immediately dispatched [edicts] to benefit the people.
translations.idiomatic: whenever something burdened the people, he promptly issued orders for their benefit.

sentences.zh: 嘗欲作露台，召匠計之，直百金。

translations.literal: He once wished to build an open-air terrace, summoned craftsmen to calculate it—the cost a hundred gold.
translations.idiomatic: He once wished to build an open terrace, summoned craftsmen to estimate it, and the cost came to a hundred gold.

sentences.zh: 上曰：「百金，中人十家之產也。

translations.literal: The Emperor said: "A hundred gold is the property of ten middling households.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor said, "A hundred gold is the estate of ten middling households.

sentences.zh: 吾奉先帝宮室，常恐羞之，何以台為！

translations.literal: I inherit the Former Emperor's palaces, constantly fearing to shame them—why build a terrace!
translations.idiomatic: I inherit the Former Emperor's palaces and constantly fear to disgrace them—why build a terrace!

sentences.zh: 」身衣弋綈；

translations.literal: " He personally wore coarse black silk;
translations.idiomatic: " He himself wore plain black silk;

sentences.zh: 所幸慎夫人，衣不曳地；

translations.literal: Consort Shen Fu whom he favored—her robes did not trail the ground;
translations.idiomatic: Lady Shen Fu, whom he favored, wore robes that did not trail the ground;

sentences.zh: 帷帳無文繡；

translations.literal: curtains and canopies had no patterned embroidery;
translations.idiomatic: curtains and canopies bore no brocade;

sentences.zh: 以示敦樸，為天下先。

translations.literal: to show earnest simplicity and be first for all under Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: to show earnest simplicity and set an example for the realm.

sentences.zh: 治霸陵，皆瓦器，不得以金、銀、銅、錫為飾，因其山，不起墳。

translations.literal: In preparing Baling tomb, all were earthenware vessels; one might not use gold, silver, copper, or tin for ornament; following the mountain, no mound was raised.
translations.idiomatic: For Baling tomb everything was earthenware; gold, silver, copper, and tin were forbidden as ornament; the mountain itself served, and no mound was raised.

sentences.zh: 吳王詐病不朝，賜以幾杖。

translations.literal: The King of Wu feigned illness and did not attend court; he was granted a folding stool and staff.
translations.idiomatic: The King of Wu feigned illness and stayed away from court; the Emperor granted him a stool and staff of exemption.

sentences.zh: 群臣袁盎等諫說雖切，常假借納用焉。

translations.literal: When the host of ministers such as Yuan Ang remonstrated urgently, he often pretended to accept and employ their advice.
translations.idiomatic: When ministers such as Yuan Ang remonstrated sharply, he often pretended to accept their counsel.

sentences.zh: 張武等受賂金錢，覺，更加賞賜以愧其心；

translations.literal: Zhang Wu and others accepted bribes in gold and cash; when discovered, he added further rewards and grants to shame their hearts;
translations.idiomatic: When Zhang Wu and others were found to have taken bribes in gold and cash, he added further rewards to shame them;

sentences.zh: 專務以德化民。

translations.literal: he devoted himself solely to transforming the people through virtue.
translations.idiomatic: he devoted himself to governing the people through virtue.

sentences.zh: 是以海內安寧，家給人足，後世鮮能及之。

translations.literal: Thus within the seas all was tranquil, households provided and people sufficed—later ages have rarely been able to match him.
translations.idiomatic: Thus the realm was tranquil, households were provided for and the people had enough—later ages have rarely matched him.

sentences.zh: ----2丁未，太子即皇帝位，尊皇太后薄氏曰太皇太后，皇后曰皇太后。

translations.literal: ----2 On dingwei, the Crown Prince took the Son of Heaven's throne; he honored the Empress Dowager Lady Bo as Grand Empress Dowager and the Empress as Empress Dowager.
translations.idiomatic: ----2 On the day dingwei the crown prince took the throne; he honored Empress Dowager Lady Bo as Grand Empress Dowager and the empress as Empress Dowager.

sentences.zh: ----3九月，有星孛於西方。

translations.literal: ----3 In the ninth month, a broom star appeared in the west.
translations.idiomatic: ----3 In the ninth month a broom star appeared in the west.

sentences.zh: ----4是歲，長沙王吳著薨，無子，國除。

translations.literal: ----4 This year King of Changsha Wu Zhu died; he had no son; the state was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: ----4 That year King Wu Zhu of Changsha died without a son, and the kingdom was abolished.

sentences.zh: 初，高祖賢文王芮，制誥御史：「長沙王忠，其令著令。

translations.literal: Earlier, Gaozu esteemed King Wen Wu Rui and made an edict to the Censor: "The King of Changsha is loyal—let this be established as a standing rule.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Gaozu esteemed King Wen Wu Rui and issued an edict to the censor: "The King of Changsha is loyal; let this be made a standing rule.

sentences.zh: 」至孝惠、高后時，封芮庶子二人為列侯，傳國數世絕。

translations.literal: " By the times of Xiaohui and Empress Dowager Gao, two of Rui's sons by concubines were enfeoffed as ranked marquises; the transmitted state passed several generations and ended.
translations.idiomatic: " Under Emperor Xiaohui and Empress Dowager Gao, two of Rui's sons by concubines were enfeoffed as marquises; the line passed several generations and died out.

sentences.zh: 1冬，十月，丞相嘉等奏：「功莫大於高皇帝，德莫盛於孝文皇帝。

translations.literal: 1. In winter, the tenth month, Chancellor Jia and others memorialized: "Merit is none greater than High Emperor's; virtue is none more abundant than Emperor Xiaowen's.
translations.idiomatic: 1. In winter, the tenth month, Chancellor Jia and others memorialized: "No merit surpasses Gaozu's; no virtue surpasses Emperor Wen's.

sentences.zh: 高皇帝廟，宜為帝者太祖之廟；

translations.literal: High Emperor's temple ought to be the dynasty's Supreme Ancestor temple;
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu's temple ought to be the dynasty's Supreme Ancestor temple;

sentences.zh: 孝文皇帝廟，宜為帝者太宗之廟。

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaowen's temple ought to be the dynasty's Grand Ancestor temple.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen's temple ought to be the dynasty's Grand Ancestor temple.

sentences.zh: 天子宜世世獻祖宗之廟，郡國諸侯宜各為孝文皇帝立太宗之廟。

translations.literal: The Son of Heaven ought generation after generation to present offerings at the Ancestors' temples; commanderies and states and feudal lords ought each to establish Emperor Xiaowen's Grand Ancestor temple.
translations.idiomatic: The Son of Heaven ought to offer at the ancestral temples generation after generation, and every commandery, kingdom, and feudal lord ought to establish Emperor Wen's Grand Ancestor temple.

sentences.zh: 」制曰：「可。

translations.literal: " An imperial rescript said: "Approved.
translations.idiomatic: " The rescript ran: "Approved.

sentences.zh: 」----2夏，四月，乙卯，赦天下。

translations.literal: " ----2 In summer, the fourth month, on yimao, he pardoned all under Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: " ----2 In summer, the fourth month, on the day yimao, he proclaimed a general amnesty.

sentences.zh: ----3遣御史大夫青至代下與匈奴和親。

translations.literal: ----3 He sent Grandee Secretary Qing to Dai's lower marches to make peace and kinship with the Xiongnu.
translations.idiomatic: ----3 He sent Grandee Secretary Qing to the lower marches of Dai to make peace with the Xiongnu.

sentences.zh: ----4五月，復收民田半租，三十而稅一。

translations.literal: ----4 In the fifth month, he again collected from the people half the field rent—one part in thirty.
translations.idiomatic: ----4 In the fifth month he again collected half the field rent from the people—one part in thirty.

sentences.zh: ----5初，文帝除肉刑，外有輕刑之名，內實殺人；

translations.literal: ----5 Earlier, Emperor Wen abolished corporal punishments; outwardly there was the name of light punishment, inwardly it actually killed people;
translations.idiomatic: ----5 Earlier Emperor Wen had abolished corporal punishments; outwardly punishments were lighter, but in practice many still died;

sentences.zh: 斬右止者又當死；

translations.literal: those whose right foot was cut off were again liable to death;
translations.idiomatic: those who had the right foot cut off were again liable to death;

sentences.zh: 斬左止者笞五百，當劓者笞三百，率多死。

translations.literal: those whose left foot was cut off were flogged five hundred strokes; those due to have the nose cut were flogged three hundred—in most cases many died.
translations.idiomatic: those who had the left foot cut off were flogged five hundred strokes; those due to have the nose cut were flogged three hundred—in most cases they died.

sentences.zh: 是歲，下詔曰：「加笞、重罪無異；

translations.literal: This year an edict ran: "Increased flogging and heavy crime are no different;
translations.idiomatic: That year an edict ran: "Increased flogging and heavy crimes are no different;

sentences.zh: 幸而不死，不可為人。

translations.literal: if fortunately not dead, one cannot function as a person.
translations.idiomatic: if by luck one does not die, one cannot live as a person.

sentences.zh: 其定律：笞五百曰三百，笞三百曰二百。

translations.literal: Let the law be fixed: flogging five hundred becomes three hundred, flogging three hundred becomes two hundred.
translations.idiomatic: Let the law be fixed: five hundred strokes become three hundred, three hundred become two hundred.

sentences.zh: 」----6以太中大夫周仁為郎中令，張歐為廷尉，楚元王子平陸侯禮為宗正，中大夫晁錯為左內史。

translations.literal: " ----6 Grand Master of the Palace Zhou Ren was made Prefect of the Gentlemen, Zhang Ou was made Commandant of Punishments, King Yuan of Chu's son Marquis of Pinglu Liu Li was made Director of the Imperial Clan, and Central Grandee Chao Cuo was made Left Administrator of the Capital.
translations.idiomatic: " ----6 Grand Master Zhou Ren was made Prefect of the Gentlemen, Zhang Ou Commandant of Punishments, King Yuan of Chu's son Marquis of Pinglu Liu Li Director of the Imperial Clan, and Central Grandee Chao Cuo Left Administrator of the Capital.

sentences.zh: 仁始為太子舍人，以廉謹得幸。

translations.literal: Ren had begun as a crown prince attendant and through incorrupt conduct and prudence gained favor.
translations.idiomatic: Ren had begun as a crown prince attendant and through incorrupt prudence gained favor.

sentences.zh: 張歐亦事帝於太子宮，雖治刑名家，為人長者，帝由是重之，用為九卿。

translations.literal: Zhang Ou also had served the Emperor in the crown prince's palace; though he studied the Legalist school of punishments and names, as a man he was an elder; the Emperor thereby valued him and used him among the Nine Ministers.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Ou had also served the Emperor in the crown prince's palace; though he studied the Legalist school of punishments, as a man he was an elder, and the Emperor valued him and made him one of the Nine Ministers.

sentences.zh: 歐為吏未嘗言按人，專以誠長者處官；

translations.literal: Ou as an officer had never spoken of investigating people; he solely took sincerity and elderhood in conducting office;
translations.idiomatic: As an officer Ou never spoke of investigating people; he governed solely through sincerity and elderhood;

sentences.zh: 官屬以為長者，亦不敢大欺。

translations.literal: his subordinates took him for an elder and also did not dare greatly deceive.
translations.idiomatic: his subordinates regarded him as an elder and did not dare greatly deceive him.

sentences.zh: ----1冬，十二月，有星孛於西南。

translations.literal: ----1 In winter, the twelfth month, a broom star appeared in the southwest.
translations.idiomatic: ----1 In winter, the twelfth month, a broom star appeared in the southwest.

sentences.zh: ----2令天下男子年二十始傅。

translations.literal: ----2 He ordered that males throughout the realm at age twenty first register for labor service.
translations.idiomatic: ----2 He ordered that males throughout the realm register for labor service at age twenty.

sentences.zh: ----3春，三月，甲寅，立皇子德為河間王，閼為臨江王，餘為淮陽王，非為汝南王，彭祖為廣川王，發為長沙王。

translations.literal: ----3 In spring, the third month, on jiayin, he installed the princes: De as King of Hejian, Que as King of Linjiang, Yu as King of Huaiyang, Fei as King of Runan, Pengzu as King of Guangchuan, Fa as King of Changsha.
translations.idiomatic: ----3 In spring, the third month, on the day jiayin, he installed his sons: De as King of Hejian, Que as King of Linjiang, Yu as King of Huaiyang, Fei as King of Runan, Pengzu as King of Guangchuan, and Fa as King of Changsha.

sentences.zh: ----4夏，四月，壬午，太皇太后薄氏崩。

translations.literal: ----4 In summer, the fourth month, on renwu, Grand Empress Dowager Lady Bo died.
translations.idiomatic: ----4 In summer, the fourth month, on the day renwu, Grand Empress Dowager Lady Bo died.

sentences.zh: ----5六月，丞相申屠嘉薨。

translations.literal: ----5 In the sixth month, Chancellor Shen Tujia died.
translations.idiomatic: ----5 In the sixth month Chancellor Shen Tujia died.

sentences.zh: 時內史晁錯數請間言事，輒聽，寵幸傾九卿，法令多所更定。

translations.literal: At this time Administrator of the Capital Chao Cuo repeatedly requested private audience on affairs—the Emperor always listened; favor and grace tilted the Nine Ministers; laws and orders were much revised.
translations.idiomatic: At this time Administrator Chao Cuo repeatedly sought private audience on affairs and was always heard; his favor eclipsed the Nine Ministers, and laws and orders were widely revised.

sentences.zh: 丞相嘉自絀所言不用，疾錯。

translations.literal: Chancellor Jia felt himself shamed, his words not employed, and hated Cuo.
translations.idiomatic: Chancellor Jia felt himself shamed when his advice went unused and hated Cuo.

sentences.zh: 錯為內史，東出不便，更穿一門南出。

translations.literal: Cuo as Administrator found going out east inconvenient and cut through another gate to exit south.
translations.idiomatic: As administrator Cuo found the eastern exit inconvenient and cut a new gate to the south.

sentences.zh: 南出者，太上皇廟堧垣也。

translations.literal: What he exited south through was the Grand Supreme Emperor temple's outer wall.
translations.idiomatic: The southern exit passed through the outer wall of the Grand Supreme Emperor's temple.

sentences.zh: 嘉聞錯穿宗廟垣，為奏，請誅錯。

translations.literal: Jia heard Cuo had cut through the ancestral temple wall, made a memorial, and requested Cuo's execution.
translations.idiomatic: Jia heard that Cuo had cut through the ancestral temple wall, memorialized, and requested Cuo's execution.

sentences.zh: 客有語錯，錯恐，夜入宮上謁，自歸上。

translations.literal: A guest told Cuo; Cuo was afraid and at night entered the palace to appear before the Emperor, surrendering himself.
translations.idiomatic: A guest warned Cuo; afraid, he entered the palace at night to present himself and surrender.

sentences.zh: 至朝，嘉請誅內史錯。

translations.literal: At court, Jia requested execution of Administrator Cuo.
translations.idiomatic: At court Jia requested that Administrator Cuo be executed.

sentences.zh: 上曰：「錯所穿非真廟垣，乃外堧垣，故冗官居其中；

translations.literal: The Emperor said: "What Cuo cut through is not the true temple wall but the outer wall, where redundant officers dwell;
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor said, "What Cuo cut through is not the true temple wall but the outer wall, where redundant officers dwell;

sentences.zh: 且又我使為之，錯無罪。

translations.literal: moreover I had him do it—Cuo has no crime.
translations.idiomatic: moreover I ordered him to do it—Cuo is guiltless.

sentences.zh: 」丞相嘉謝。

translations.literal: " Chancellor Jia apologized.
translations.idiomatic: " Chancellor Jia apologized.

sentences.zh: 罷朝，嘉謂長史曰：「吾悔不先斬錯乃請之，為錯所賣。

translations.literal: Court dismissed, Jia said to his chief clerk: "I regret I did not first behead Cuo before requesting it—I was sold by Cuo.
translations.idiomatic: After court Jia told his chief clerk, "I regret I did not behead Cuo first before requesting it—I was outmaneuvered by Cuo.

sentences.zh: 」至舍，因歐血而死。

translations.literal: " When he reached his residence, he consequently vomited blood and died.
translations.idiomatic: " When he reached his residence he vomited blood and died.

sentences.zh: 錯以此愈貴。

translations.literal: Cuo thereby became still more exalted.
translations.idiomatic: Cuo thereby became still more exalted.

sentences.zh: ----6秋，與匈奴和親。

translations.literal: ----6 In autumn, peace and kinship with the Xiongnu.
translations.idiomatic: ----6 In autumn the court made peace with the Xiongnu.

sentences.zh: ----7八月，丁未，以御史大夫開封侯陶青為丞相。

translations.literal: ----7 In the eighth month, on dingwei, Grandee Secretary Marquis of Kaifeng Tao Qing was made Chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: ----7 In the eighth month, on the day dingwei, Grandee Secretary Marquis of Kaifeng Tao Qing was made Chancellor.

sentences.zh: 丁巳，以內史晁錯為御史大夫。

translations.literal: On dingsi, Administrator of the Capital Chao Cuo was made Grandee Secretary.
translations.idiomatic: On the day dingsi Administrator Chao Cuo was made Grandee Secretary.

sentences.zh: ----8彗星出東北。

translations.literal: ----8 A comet appeared in the northeast.
translations.idiomatic: ----8 A comet appeared in the northeast.

sentences.zh: ----9秋，衡山雨雹，大者五寸，深者二尺。

translations.literal: ----9 In autumn, Hengshan had hail—the large ones five inches, depth in places two feet.
translations.idiomatic: ----9 In autumn Hengshan had hail as large as five inches across and piled two feet deep in places.

sentences.zh: ----10熒惑逆行守北辰，月出北辰間；

translations.literal: ----10 Mars moved retrograde and guarded the North Pole; the moon emerged between the North Pole stars;
translations.idiomatic: ----10 Mars moved retrograde and guarded the North Pole; the moon passed between the North Pole stars;

sentences.zh: 歲星逆行天廷中。

translations.literal: Jupiter moved retrograde within the Celestial Court.
translations.idiomatic: Jupiter moved retrograde within the Celestial Court.

sentences.zh: ----11梁孝王以竇太后少子故，有寵，王四十餘城，居天下膏腴地。

translations.literal: ----11 King Xiao of Liang because he was Empress Dowager Dou's youngest son had favor; he ruled more than forty cities and occupied the realm's richest lands.
translations.idiomatic: ----11 King Xiao of Liang, as Empress Dowager Dou's youngest son, was favored; he ruled more than forty cities on the richest lands in the realm.

sentences.zh: 賞賜不可勝道，府庫金錢且百巨萬，珠玉寶器多於京師。

translations.literal: Rewards and grants beyond reckoning; treasury gold and cash nearly a hundred hundred-thousands; pearls, jade, and precious vessels more than in the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Rewards and grants were beyond reckoning; his treasury held nearly ten million in gold and cash, and pearls, jade, and precious vessels outnumbered those in the capital.

sentences.zh: 築東苑，方三百餘里，廣睢陽城七十里，大治宮室，為覆道，自宮連屬於平台三十餘里。

translations.literal: He built the Eastern Park, three hundred-odd li square; expanded Suiyang city seventy li; greatly built palaces; made covered passages from the palace linked continuously to the Terrace Platform for more than thirty li.
translations.idiomatic: He built the Eastern Park, more than three hundred li square; expanded Suiyang city seventy li; greatly enlarged his palaces; and made covered passages linking the palace to the Terrace Platform for more than thirty li.

sentences.zh: 招延四方豪俊之士，如吳人枚乘、嚴忌，齊人羊勝、公孫詭、鄒陽，蜀人司馬相如之屬皆從之游。

translations.literal: He invited and retained eminent men from the four quarters—such as Wu men Mei Sheng and Yan Ji, Qi men Yang Sheng, Gongsun Gui, and Zou Yang, Shu man Sima Xiangru and their sort—all followed and associated with him.
translations.idiomatic: He gathered eminent men from the four quarters—such as Wu's Mei Sheng and Yan Ji, Qi's Yang Sheng, Gongsun Gui, and Zou Yang, and Shu's Sima Xiangru and their like—all of whom associated with him.

sentences.zh: 每入朝，上使使持節以乘輿駟馬迎梁王於關下。

translations.literal: Each time he entered court, the Emperor sent an envoy bearing credentials with the imperial carriage's four-horse team to welcome the King of Liang below the passes.
translations.idiomatic: Each time he came to court the Emperor sent an envoy with credentials and the imperial four-horse carriage to welcome the King of Liang below the passes.

sentences.zh: 既至，寵幸無比，入則侍上同輦，出則同車，射獵上林中。

translations.literal: Once arrived, favor and grace had no peer—entering he attended the Emperor sharing the carriage; leaving they shared the same chariot, hunting in the Shanglin Park.
translations.idiomatic: Once he arrived his favor had no peer: entering court he rode with the Emperor in the same carriage; leaving they shared the same chariot and hunted in the Shanglin Park.

sentences.zh: 因上疏請留，且半歲。

translations.literal: He then submitted a memorial requesting to remain—nearly half a year.
translations.idiomatic: He then submitted a memorial asking to remain—nearly half a year.

sentences.zh: 梁侍中、郎、謁者著籍引出入天子殿門，與漢宦官無異。

translations.literal: Liang's palace attendants, gentlemen, and ushers were entered in registers to lead in and out through the Son of Heaven's palace gates—no different from Han eunuch officers.
translations.idiomatic: Liang's attendants, gentlemen, and ushers were entered in registers to pass in and out of the Son of Heaven's palace gates—no different from Han palace eunuchs.
